# Background

The Cassia Crossbill (*Loxia sinesciuris*) is Idaho's only endemic species whose limited range and diet put the species at risk for extinction (*FIND CITATIONS FROM NWCASC ADVISOR GRANT RE: IDFWS AND CACR STATUS*; Parmesan 2006, Benkman 1993). Similar to other crossbills whose crossed mandibles aid in prying open the conifer cones of a single species (or a variety of species) to then forage on the seeds inside (Newton 1972, Benkman 1978a, Benkman 1978b, Benkman 1988a, Benkman 1988b, Benkman 1989, Benkman 1990, Benkman 1992, Benkman 1993, Benkman and Lindholm 1991). Cassia Crossbills feed almost exclusively on the serotinous cones of Rocky Mountain lodgepole pine (*Pinus contorta latifolia*) and are unable to survive competition with other crossbills for other seeds elsewhere (Benkman et al. 2001, Benkman et al. 2012, Benkman 2016). Unlike the far more common Red Crossbill (*Loxia curvirostra*) that are nomadic and able to travel vast distances for food, the Cassia Crossbill have a highly restricted range limited to the 67km2 of Rocky Mountain lodgepole pine forest found on two small mountain ranges in Idaho: the South Hills and the Albion Mountains (Benkman et al. 2009, Behl and Benkman 2018; Figure 1). Despite lodgepole pine existing in other areas, the Cassia Crossbill was able to evolve in this region due to the lack of red squirrels (*Tamiasciurus hudsonicus*) which typically preemptively out-compete crossbills for cones (Benkman 1999, Smith and Benkman 2007).

![Figure 1: Map showing the South Hills and Albion Mountain range. The white outline marks the boundary of the Sawtooth National Forest](C:/Users/britt/OneDrive/Pictures/CassiaSites1.png)

The combination of being a permanent resident restricted to high elevation environments and dependent on a singular resource makes the Cassia Crossbill extremely sensitive to habitat alteration or loss (Benkman 1993). For example, in 2020 the Badger Fire swept through the western portion of the South Hills and destroyed approximately 20% of the available lodgepole in the region. In subsequent years, annual trends in the population declines significantly (*FIND CITATION FROM NW CASC GRANTS OR ANNUAL REPORTS & FIGURES*). Wildfires in this region -like many other areas in the western US - are predicted to increase in frequency and intensity in the future (Brice et al. 2020, Rogers et al. 2020). Wildfires can damage or destroy the mature stands of lodgepole pine which contain the serotinous cones - cones sealed in a resin - that Cassia Crossbills forage on. However, when these areas experience stand-replacing fires the resin on the serotinous cones melts and seeds inside have the potential to germinate and create a new stand. Serotinous cones in this region may also be affected by high summer temperatures which some evidence has shown to cause these cones to open prematurely and allowing other species to access a once exclusive resource (Benkman et al. 2001, Benkman et al. 2012, Santisteban et al. 2012, Benkman 2016).

# Data Inspection

Originally, I was using lidRviewer package in R to visually inspect the areas to see if they matched areas I had been to. However, given my storage, it wasn't possible to load the subset of tiles fully without overloading my computer or R's memory. To resolve this, I am doing a quick look over of the tiles in RStudio to quickly get a sense of whether they look natural and if they match up with the area they are intended to represent. After, the full tile is removed so I can inspect the next one. Then the full tiles are loaded into CloudCompare (version 2.13.2) for a better quality assessment to check the density patterns, canopy penetration, and ground realism. Once tiles are assess, we can configure the pipeline for filtering, classification, and generating forest metrics.

**Note: code chunks are not set to run to avoid issues with memory. Rather code chunks should only display code for reproducibility. Additionally, screenshots of CloudCompare areas were saved to compare densities and for reproducibility.** Commands:

-   Rotate with left mouse button

-   Zoom with mouse wheel

-   Pan with right mouse button

-   Keyboard r or g or b to color with RGB

-   Keyboard z to color with Z

-   Keyboard i to color with Intensity

-   Keyboard c to color with Classification

-   Keyboard + or - to change the point size

-   Keyboard l to enable/disable eyes-dome lightning

Since I am using the raw point cloud, we are likely to see withheld and synthetic classified points. *Note: reasoning for withholding 'withheld' points:*

-   *they are points the data provider recommends you ignore*

-   *overlap in flight lines*

-   *edge-of-scan artifacts*

-   *points kept for QA but not analysis*

-   *points excluded from the official product*

*I am keeping the synthetic points because:*

-   *adds improved surface continuity*

-   *points are generated during processing*

-   *densified surfaces in workflows*

Based on this information, we should reclassify these tiles. We should begin by working with these tiles to create a general pipeline for classification (which we can then use the **batch** function to do to all tiles).

# Pipeline Code (Clipped Tiles)

Here our goal is to create a pipeline by generating code using these 3 tiles. We should then be able to batch these to other tiles in the study area. Process steps:

1.  Noise Filter - start with this in case there are unusual noise below ground (may accidentally create weird geometry and makes ground classification more stable)

2.  Classify Ground Points

3.  Second cleanup of noise - if needed

4.  Generate a Normalized Canopy Height Model

## Create Catalog for Pipeline

**To do this step and save memory, we are going to create a small catalog of our earlier tiles to represent different densities, slopes, and regions in order to test whether the pipeline fails to accommodate any of these things. We will use the following 8 tiles:**

-   *Logger LPO-034 & Logger LPO-130 - Elko*

-   *Porcupine Springs Camp - Elko*

-   *Diamondfield Jack Camp - Southern ID 2018 #12*

-   *Known location - Southern ID 2018 #12*

-   *Reference 3 - Southern ID 2018 #14*

-   *Reference 2 - Southern ID 2018 #15*

-   *Independence Lake - Southern ID 2018 #17*

-   *Logger LPO-060 - Southern ID #17*

```{r Create Pipeline Catalog}

# Create a path to the files 

pipeline_files <- c(
  "R:/ElkoNW_LAZ/USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG260710.laz",
  "R:/ElkoNW_LAZ/USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG305605.laz",
  "R:/Part22/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG230725.laz",
  "R:/Part21/Part21/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG380725.laz",
  "R:/SouthernIdaho2018_14_LAZ/SouthernIdaho2018_14_LAZ/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_12TTM850725.laz",
  "R:/07_Cassia/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG440830.laz",
  "R:/LAZ/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_12TTM790770.laz",
  "R:/LAZ/USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_12TTM745695.laz"
  ) # Order: Porcupine Springs Camp, Logger LPO-034 & Logger LPO-130, Diamondfield Jack Camp, Known location (SID 2018 - 12), SID 2018 - 14 reference 3, SID 2018 - 15 reference 2, Independence Lake Camp, and Logger LPO-060 
  
# Normalize the Paths

pipeline_files <- normalizePath(pipeline_files, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

# Create Catalog
ctg_test <- readLAScatalog(pipeline_files)

# Check Catalog
ctg_test

# Make a bounding box in the center of each tile for efficiency

df <- ctg_test@data
names(df)

box_size <- 500
half <- box_size / 2

qa_boxes <- data.frame(
  name = paste0("tile", seq_len(nrow(df))),   # tile1..tile8
  xmin = (df$Min.X + df$Max.X)/2 - half,
  xmax = (df$Min.X + df$Max.X)/2 + half,
  ymin = (df$Min.Y + df$Max.Y)/2 - half,
  ymax = (df$Min.Y + df$Max.Y)/2 + half
)


qa_boxes

# Create a bounding box to intersect tile
qa_polys <- st_sfc(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(qa_boxes)), function(i) {
    st_polygon(list(matrix(c(
      qa_boxes$xmin[i], qa_boxes$ymin[i],
      qa_boxes$xmax[i], qa_boxes$ymin[i],
      qa_boxes$xmax[i], qa_boxes$ymax[i],
      qa_boxes$xmin[i], qa_boxes$ymax[i],
      qa_boxes$xmin[i], qa_boxes$ymin[i]
    ), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)))
  }),
  crs = st_crs(ctg_test)
)

qa_polys <- st_sf(name = qa_boxes$name, geometry = qa_polys)

# Intersect Tile to BB
ctg_qa <- catalog_intersect(ctg_test, qa_polys)
ctg_qa

sf::st_crs(ctg_test)
sf::st_crs(qa_polys)


plot(ctg_test)
plot(sf::st_geometry(qa_polys), add = TRUE, border = "red", lwd = 2)

```

## Filter Noise

When looking at the datasets there are some obvious levels of noise (in fact the amount of noise increased with each tile we examined). Filtering out these extraneous high and low (below the scene) points will help to reduce error and get us closer to the actual landscape. Note: this is only using distance to neighboring points/returns and no use of scan angle/intensity

First let's try the **ivf (isolated voxel function)** from lidR to filter the noise by searching the returns for ones that are far away from neighbors.Let's try using a filter where we filter points that are no more than 12 returns within a resolution of 4m. We then filter the points by removing those that are classified as noise (the LASNOISE = 7 and 18).

Overall, we we should check if the IVF being too strict by either counting how many points were removed. Commonly, \< 1-2% is fine but anything greater than 5% should be looked at visually. We will also visually check the filters to see if they were appropriate and we may play with parameters to see which produces the best result.

Additionally, we will be filtering the withheld and synthetic flagged points since they are not recommended for use as they could create bias in our data.

Here we will use the catalog to save space in R and RAM.

```{r Generate Filter Pipeline - Center Boundary Box 500m}
# Set the number of threads to reduce RAM spikes
lidR::set_lidr_threads(1)

# Output folder
out_dir <- "Output_Files/Filter_Chunks/"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(length(pipeline_files) == nrow(qa_boxes))

for (k in seq_along(pipeline_files)) {

  f <- pipeline_files[k]
  base <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  out_file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(base, "_center500_filtered.laz"))

  message("\n[", k, "/", length(pipeline_files), "] ", base)

  # Skip if already done
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    message("  -> already exists, skipping: ", out_file)
    next
  }

  # Read full tile
  las <- readLAS(f)
  if (is.empty(las)) {
    message("  -> tile is empty, skipping")
    rm(las); gc()
    next
  }

  # Clip 500x500 center box for THIS tile
  clip <- clip_rectangle(
    las,
    xleft   = qa_boxes$xmin[k],
    ybottom = qa_boxes$ymin[k],
    xright  = qa_boxes$xmax[k],
    ytop    = qa_boxes$ymax[k]
  )

  # Free full tile ASAP
  rm(las); gc()

  if (is.empty(clip)) {
    message("  -> clip is empty, skipping")
    rm(clip); gc()
    next
  }

  # Filter pipeline on the clip
  clip <- filter_poi(clip, !Withheld_flag & !Synthetic_flag)
  clip <- classify_noise(clip, ivf(res = 4, n = 12))
  clip <- filter_poi(clip, !Classification %in% c(7L, 18L))

  if (is.empty(clip)) {
    message("  -> clip became empty after filtering, skipping")
    rm(clip); gc()
    next
  }

  # Write output
  writeLAS(clip, out_file)
  message("  -> wrote: ", out_file, " (n=", npoints(clip), ")")

  # Cleanup
  rm(clip); gc()
}


```

We will then check the chunks in CloudCompare to ensure there isn't any canopy shearing or noise left behind.

## Fix CRS Discrepancy

Found there were multiple CRS, so we will want to account for this and run them under different sections

Working in mountainous forests, we will need to keep track of the parameters that we use. It is standard to use a cloth simulation filter which is available through the LiDAR function csf(). With the csf function, the LiDAR point cloud is inverted, and a simulation of a “rigid cloth” is draped over the inverted point cloud. The simulated cloth surface is then used to determine which points are associated with the ground.

CSF is controlled by:

-   how stiff the 'cloth' is --\> rigidity

-   how coarse the 'cloth' mesh is --\> cloth resolution

-   much much sagging is allowed --\> slope smoothing

Cloth Resolution typical values:

-   0.5 - 0.75 m = very fine cloth (captures small terrain detail)

-   1 m = medium cloth (balanced)

-   2–3 m = coarse cloth (very smooth terrain)

For our data set we have moderate-to-high density, so we could try 0.5m if 1m isn't working well. The smaller values (0.5m) typically is recommended for dense canopy, complex terrain, and reduces over-smoothing. However, it can eat a lot of RAM and run much slower.

Rigidness typical values:

-   1 = flexible cloth (follows small bumps)
-   2 = balanced (good starting point)
-   3 = very stiff (smooth terrain)

Class Threshold typical values:

-   0.3 = stricter ground and may miss true ground under canopy
-   0.5 = good starting point and mid-range
-   0.7 - 1 = risk classifying low vegetation as ground

We will also be trying the PMF (progressive morphological filter) which creates a small window and finds the low points where it then gradually increases the window size and allow higher thresholds as terrain scale increases.Then, we will compare the two. I expect that the CSF may perform better compared to the PMF due to the mountainous terrain.

PMF is controlled by:

-   window size(s) (scale of terrain features)

-   height threshold (how much deviation from the ground is allowed)

**Here we will begin with starting with the default then check the DTM and tune from there. Since we are classifying these ourselves, we should be on the lookout for DTM pits, sinks, or 'wavy' terrain**

Window Size Typical Values:

-   3-5 = small to detect micro-terrain but may misclassify roots/rocks
-   5-10 = balanced (good default)
-   10+ = large for very smooth but can miss real terrain detail

Height Threshold Typical Values:

-   0.5-1.0 = flat terrain
-   1.0-2.0 = forested terrain
-   1.5-3.0 = steep/mountainous

Once points are classified, you know which points are associated with the ground, but because points are not continuous on the ground, you still need to interpolate between them to get an elevation map. For this, you can use a Delaunay triangulation which interpolates a continuous surface as a triangulation between the points classified as ground. You can implement the triangulation using the rasterize_terrain() function in the lidR package with the tin() algorithm selected.

```{r Generate Ground Classification Pipeline - Center Boundary Box 500m}


############# Set up Tiles (Do NOT run if you are running the previous chunk above and it is loaded into the environment) #############

# I had to close R so I need to find the filtered 500m centered ROI clips (so I do not need to re-run the filter)

## Create Shared Helper Functions and Settings

This will help keep things flowing and reduce redundancy as we create metrics.

```{r Shared Helper Functions and Settings - Pipeline}
##### Define Shared Helper Functions #####
# Put all small helper functions in one place so the downstream steps read cleanly

extract_tile_key_from_path <- function(single_norm_path) {
  file_stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_norm_path))

  # Standard spatial tile code pattern such as 11TQG335770
  matched_pattern <- regexpr("\\b\\d{2}[A-Z]{3}\\d{6}\\b", file_stem, perl = TRUE)

  if (matched_pattern[1] != -1) {
    return(regmatches(file_stem, matched_pattern)[1])
  }

  # Fallback: remove long processing suffix if present
  file_stem <- sub("_center500_filtered_.*$", "", file_stem)

  # Final fallback: truncate long names
  substr(file_stem, 1, 60)
}

safe_write_raster <- function(single_raster, output_filename) {
  tryCatch(
    terra::writeRaster(single_raster, filename = output_filename, overwrite = TRUE),
    error = function(e) {
      stop(
        "writeRaster failed for:\n  ",
        output_filename,
        "\nReason: ",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
    }
  )
}

replace_na_inf_with_zero <- function(single_raster) {
  raster_values <- terra::values(single_raster, mat = FALSE)
  raster_values[is.na(raster_values)] <- 0
  raster_values[!is.finite(raster_values)] <- 0
  terra::values(single_raster) <- raster_values
  single_raster
}

safe_p95_function <- function(z_values) {
  if (length(z_values) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(stats::quantile(z_values, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE, type = 7))
}

safe_complexity_function <- function(z_values) {
  if (length(z_values) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  mean_height_value <- mean(z_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_height_value <- stats::sd(z_values, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (!is.finite(mean_height_value) || mean_height_value <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  if (!is.finite(sd_height_value)) return(NA_real_)

  sd_height_value / mean_height_value
}

safe_fhd_function <- function(bin_proportions) {
  valid_proportions <- bin_proportions[is.finite(bin_proportions) & bin_proportions > 0]

  if (length(valid_proportions) == 0) {
    return(0)
  }

  -sum(valid_proportions * log(valid_proportions))
}


##### Define Shared Step Settings #####
# Keep all major parameter settings together so they are easy to audit/change

vertical_resolution_m <- 5
vertical_cell_area_m2 <- vertical_resolution_m * vertical_resolution_m

height_bin_definitions <- list(
  bin_0to2m   = c(0, 2),
  bin_2to5m   = c(2, 5),
  bin_5to10m  = c(5, 10),
  bin_10mplus = c(10, Inf)
)

# Cover is broad vegetation cover above 2 m
cover_height_threshold_m <- 2

# CHM focal smoothing window
chm_focal_window_matrix_3x3 <- matrix(1, nrow = 3, ncol = 3)

# Cover focal smoothing window
cover_focal_window_matrix_3x3 <- matrix(1, nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
apply_cover_focal_smoothing <- TRUE

# Force terra temp files into a known writable location
terra_temp_directory <- file.path(output_root_directory, "terra_tmp")
dir.create(terra_temp_directory, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
terra::terraOptions(tempdir = terra_temp_directory)

stopifnot(dir.exists(terra_temp_directory))
stopifnot(file.access(terra_temp_directory, 2) == 0)

```

## Forest Metrics

```{r Forest Metrics - Pipeline}
##### Compute Vertical Bins Cover And Bin Metrics #####

# PURPOSE:
# - This is now the main structural-metrics step
# - It writes:
#   - summary rasters
#   - per-bin density / percent / presence
#   - per-bin meanZ / sdZ / p95Z for 2-5, 5-10, and 10+
#
# IMPORTANT LOGIC:
# vegetation = Classification != 2 and Z > 0
# density / percent / presence / cover use 0 for empty cells
# height summary rasters remain NA when no points exist in that bin
# 0-2 m gets NO meanZ / sdZ / p95Z
# percent denominator = all vegetation points above 0 m in that pixel

compute_and_write_vertical_bin_metrics <- function(single_norm_path, vertical_bins_directory_list) {

  ##### Load Normalized LAS #####

  normalized_las_object <- lidR::readLAS(single_norm_path)

  if (lidR::is.empty(normalized_las_object)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  tile_key <- extract_tile_key_from_path(single_norm_path)
  message("Running Step 10 for tile: ", tile_key)

  summary_directory <- normalizePath(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$summary,
    winslash = "\\",
    mustWork = TRUE
  )

  ##### Create Template Grid #####

  # The template grid gives us the target geometry for all rasters.
  # We use all points here ONLY to establish grid alignment.
  template_count_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
    normalized_las_object,
    ~length(Z),
    res = vertical_resolution_m
  )

  if (terra::ncell(template_count_raster) == 0) {
    message("  SKIP: empty template grid for tile ", tile_key)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  ##### Select Vegetation Points #####

  vegetation_points_las <- lidR::filter_poi(
    normalized_las_object,
    Classification != 2L & Z > 0
  )

  ##### Compute Total Vegetation Count Raster #####

  if (lidR::is.empty(vegetation_points_las)) {

    vegetation_count_raster <- template_count_raster
    terra::values(vegetation_count_raster) <- 0

  } else {

    vegetation_count_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
      vegetation_points_las,
      ~length(Z),
      res = vertical_resolution_m
    )

    if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, vegetation_count_raster, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
      vegetation_count_raster <- terra::resample(
        vegetation_count_raster,
        template_count_raster,
        method = "near"
      )
    }

    vegetation_count_raster <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(vegetation_count_raster)
  }

  safe_write_raster(
    vegetation_count_raster,
    file.path(summary_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_vegcount_5m.tif"))
  )

  ##### Compute Total Vegetation Density Raster #####

  vegetation_density_total_raster <- vegetation_count_raster / vertical_cell_area_m2
  vegetation_density_total_raster <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(vegetation_density_total_raster)

  safe_write_raster(
    vegetation_density_total_raster,
    file.path(summary_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_dens_veg_total_5m.tif"))
  )

  ##### Compute Broad Vegetation Cover Raster #####

  # Cover is based on first returns only:
  # (# first-return veg points above 2 m) / (# first-return veg points above 0 m)

  first_return_vegetation_las <- normalized_las_object

  if ("ReturnNumber" %in% names(first_return_vegetation_las@data)) {
    first_return_vegetation_las <- lidR::filter_poi(first_return_vegetation_las, ReturnNumber == 1L)
  }

  first_return_vegetation_las <- lidR::filter_poi(
    first_return_vegetation_las,
    Classification != 2L & Z > 0
  )

  if (lidR::is.empty(first_return_vegetation_las)) {

    cover_raster_5m <- template_count_raster
    terra::values(cover_raster_5m) <- 0

  } else {

    cover_raster_5m <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
      first_return_vegetation_las,
      ~ ifelse(length(Z) == 0, 0, sum(Z > cover_height_threshold_m) / length(Z)),
      res = vertical_resolution_m
    )

    if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, cover_raster_5m, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
      cover_raster_5m <- terra::resample(
        cover_raster_5m,
        template_count_raster,
        method = "near"
      )
    }

    cover_raster_5m <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(cover_raster_5m)
  }

  safe_write_raster(
    cover_raster_5m,
    file.path(summary_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_cover_5m.tif"))
  )

  ##### Compute Smoothed Cover Raster #####

  if (isTRUE(apply_cover_focal_smoothing)) {

    cover_focal_mean_raster_5m <- terra::focal(
      cover_raster_5m,
      w = cover_focal_window_matrix_3x3,
      fun = mean,
      na.policy = "omit",
      fillvalue = NA
    )

    cover_focal_mean_raster_5m <- terra::clamp(
      cover_focal_mean_raster_5m,
      lower = 0,
      upper = 1,
      values = TRUE
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      cover_focal_mean_raster_5m,
      file.path(summary_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_cover_f3_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  ##### Loop Through Vertical Bins #####

  for (single_bin_name in names(height_bin_definitions)) {

    single_bin_limits <- height_bin_definitions[[single_bin_name]]
    single_bin_lower_z <- single_bin_limits[1]
    single_bin_upper_z <- single_bin_limits[2]

    single_bin_points_las <- lidR::filter_poi(
      vegetation_points_las,
      Z >= single_bin_lower_z & Z < single_bin_upper_z
    )

    single_bin_output_directory <- switch(
      single_bin_name,
      bin_0to2m   = vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_0to2m,
      bin_2to5m   = vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_2to5m,
      bin_5to10m  = vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_5to10m,
      bin_10mplus = vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_10mplus
    )

    ##### Initialize Raster Shells #####

    single_bin_count_raster <- template_count_raster
    single_bin_presence_raster <- template_count_raster
    single_bin_mean_z_raster <- template_count_raster
    single_bin_sd_z_raster <- template_count_raster
    single_bin_p95_z_raster <- template_count_raster

    terra::values(single_bin_count_raster) <- 0
    terra::values(single_bin_presence_raster) <- 0
    terra::values(single_bin_mean_z_raster) <- NA_real_
    terra::values(single_bin_sd_z_raster) <- NA_real_
    terra::values(single_bin_p95_z_raster) <- NA_real_

    ##### Populate Bin Count And Presence #####

    if (!lidR::is.empty(single_bin_points_las)) {

      single_bin_count_temp_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
        single_bin_points_las,
        ~length(Z),
        res = vertical_resolution_m
      )

      if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, single_bin_count_temp_raster, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
        single_bin_count_temp_raster <- terra::resample(
          single_bin_count_temp_raster,
          template_count_raster,
          method = "near"
        )
      }

      terra::values(single_bin_count_raster) <- terra::values(single_bin_count_temp_raster)

      single_bin_presence_raster <- single_bin_count_raster
      single_bin_presence_values <- terra::values(single_bin_presence_raster, mat = FALSE)
      single_bin_presence_values[is.na(single_bin_presence_values)] <- 0
      single_bin_presence_values[single_bin_presence_values > 0] <- 1
      terra::values(single_bin_presence_raster) <- single_bin_presence_values

      ##### Populate Height Summaries For 2m+ Bins #####

      if (single_bin_name != "bin_0to2m") {

        single_bin_mean_temp_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
          single_bin_points_las,
          ~mean(Z),
          res = vertical_resolution_m
        )

        single_bin_sd_temp_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
          single_bin_points_las,
          ~stats::sd(Z),
          res = vertical_resolution_m
        )

        single_bin_p95_temp_raster <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
          single_bin_points_las,
          ~safe_p95_function(Z),
          res = vertical_resolution_m
        )

        if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, single_bin_mean_temp_raster, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
          single_bin_mean_temp_raster <- terra::resample(
            single_bin_mean_temp_raster,
            template_count_raster,
            method = "near"
          )
        }

        if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, single_bin_sd_temp_raster, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
          single_bin_sd_temp_raster <- terra::resample(
            single_bin_sd_temp_raster,
            template_count_raster,
            method = "near"
          )
        }

        if (!terra::compareGeom(template_count_raster, single_bin_p95_temp_raster, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
          single_bin_p95_temp_raster <- terra::resample(
            single_bin_p95_temp_raster,
            template_count_raster,
            method = "near"
          )
        }

        terra::values(single_bin_mean_z_raster) <- terra::values(single_bin_mean_temp_raster)
        terra::values(single_bin_sd_z_raster) <- terra::values(single_bin_sd_temp_raster)
        terra::values(single_bin_p95_z_raster) <- terra::values(single_bin_p95_temp_raster)
      }
    }

    ##### Compute Bin Density Percent And Presence #####

    single_bin_count_raster <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(single_bin_count_raster)

    single_bin_density_raster <- single_bin_count_raster / vertical_cell_area_m2
    single_bin_density_raster <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(single_bin_density_raster)

    single_bin_percent_raster <- single_bin_count_raster / vegetation_count_raster
    single_bin_percent_raster <- replace_na_inf_with_zero(single_bin_percent_raster)

    ##### Write Bin Outputs #####

    safe_write_raster(
      single_bin_density_raster,
      file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_dens_5m.tif"))
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      single_bin_percent_raster,
      file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_pct_5m.tif"))
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      single_bin_presence_raster,
      file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_present_5m.tif"))
    )

    if (single_bin_name != "bin_0to2m") {
      safe_write_raster(
        single_bin_mean_z_raster,
        file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_meanZ_5m.tif"))
      )

      safe_write_raster(
        single_bin_sd_z_raster,
        file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_sdZ_5m.tif"))
      )

      safe_write_raster(
        single_bin_p95_z_raster,
        file.path(single_bin_output_directory, paste0(tile_key, "_p95Z_5m.tif"))
      )
    }
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}


##### Run Vertical Bin Metrics #####

##### QA Check That Bin Percent Rasters Sum To About 1 #####
# Where vegetation exists, the four bin percentages should sum to ~1
# This is an important integrity check for the vertical-distribution step

qa_check_vertical_bin_percent_sum <- function(
  vertical_bins_directory_list,
  summary_directory = vertical_bins_directory_list$summary,
  tolerance = 0.02
) {

  bin_0to2_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_0to2m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_2to5_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_2to5m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_5to10_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_5to10m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_10plus_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_10mplus,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(length(bin_0to2_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_2to5_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_5to10_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_10plus_percent_paths) > 0)

  extract_id_from_pct_filename <- function(file_path) {
    sub("_pct_5m\\.tif$", "", basename(file_path), ignore.case = TRUE)
  }

  ids_bin_0to2 <- vapply(bin_0to2_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_2to5 <- vapply(bin_2to5_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_5to10 <- vapply(bin_5to10_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_10plus <- vapply(bin_10plus_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))

  common_tile_ids <- Reduce(
    intersect,
    list(ids_bin_0to2, ids_bin_2to5, ids_bin_5to10, ids_bin_10plus)
  )

  if (length(common_tile_ids) == 0) {
    stop("No matching percent-raster sets found across the four bins.")
  }

  message("QA found ", length(common_tile_ids), " tile sets with all four percent rasters.")

  for (single_tile_id in common_tile_ids) {

    bin_0to2_raster <- terra::rast(bin_0to2_percent_paths[ids_bin_0to2 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_2to5_raster <- terra::rast(bin_2to5_percent_paths[ids_bin_2to5 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_5to10_raster <- terra::rast(bin_5to10_percent_paths[ids_bin_5to10 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_10plus_raster <- terra::rast(bin_10plus_percent_paths[ids_bin_10plus == single_tile_id][1])

    summed_bin_percent_raster <- bin_0to2_raster + bin_2to5_raster + bin_5to10_raster + bin_10plus_raster
    absolute_error_raster <- abs(summed_bin_percent_raster - 1)

    vegetation_count_path <- file.path(summary_directory, paste0(single_tile_id, "_vegcount_5m.tif"))
    vegetation_count_raster <- if (file.exists(vegetation_count_path)) terra::rast(vegetation_count_path) else NULL

    if (!is.null(vegetation_count_raster)) {
      valid_vegetation_mask <- vegetation_count_raster > 0
    } else {
      valid_vegetation_mask <- !is.na(summed_bin_percent_raster)
    }

    summed_values <- terra::values(summed_bin_percent_raster, mat = FALSE)
    absolute_error_values <- terra::values(absolute_error_raster, mat = FALSE)
    mask_values <- terra::values(valid_vegetation_mask, mat = FALSE)

    valid_index <- which(!is.na(summed_values) & !is.na(mask_values) & mask_values)

    if (length(valid_index) == 0) {
      message("QA SKIP: no valid vegetation pixels for tile ", single_tile_id)
      next
    }

    mean_sum_value <- mean(summed_values[valid_index], na.rm = TRUE)
    max_abs_error_value <- max(absolute_error_values[valid_index], na.rm = TRUE)
    percent_bad_pixels <- mean(absolute_error_values[valid_index] > tolerance, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

    message(
      "QA ",
      single_tile_id,
      " | mean(sum)=",
      round(mean_sum_value, 4),
      " | max|sum-1|=",
      round(max_abs_error_value, 4),
      " | %pixels>|tol|=",
      round(percent_bad_pixels, 2),
      "%"
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      summed_bin_percent_raster,
      file.path(summary_directory, paste0(single_tile_id, "_QA_binsum_pct_5m.tif"))
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      absolute_error_raster,
      file.path(summary_directory, paste0(single_tile_id, "_QA_binsum_absErr_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}

qa_check_vertical_bin_percent_sum(utm11_dirs$vertical_bins_5m)
qa_check_vertical_bin_percent_sum(utm12_dirs$vertical_bins_5m)


##### Compute Foliar Height Diversity From Bin Percent Rasters #####
# FHD is computed from the proportional distribution of vegetation among bins using the percent rasters generated above
# INTERPRETATION:
# low values = vegetation concentrated in fewer layers
# high values = vegetation distributed more evenly among layers

compute_fhd_from_vertical_bin_percent_rasters <- function(vertical_bins_directory_list, output_folder_path) {

  bin_0to2_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_0to2m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_2to5_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_2to5m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_5to10_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_5to10m,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  bin_10plus_percent_paths <- list.files(
    vertical_bins_directory_list$bin_10mplus,
    pattern = "_pct_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(length(bin_0to2_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_2to5_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_5to10_percent_paths) > 0)
  stopifnot(length(bin_10plus_percent_paths) > 0)

  extract_id_from_pct_filename <- function(file_path) {
    sub("_pct_5m\\.tif$", "", basename(file_path), ignore.case = TRUE)
  }

  ids_bin_0to2 <- vapply(bin_0to2_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_2to5 <- vapply(bin_2to5_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_5to10 <- vapply(bin_5to10_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))
  ids_bin_10plus <- vapply(bin_10plus_percent_paths, extract_id_from_pct_filename, character(1))

  common_tile_ids <- Reduce(
    intersect,
    list(ids_bin_0to2, ids_bin_2to5, ids_bin_5to10, ids_bin_10plus)
  )

  stopifnot(length(common_tile_ids) > 0)

  for (single_tile_id in common_tile_ids) {

    bin_0to2_raster <- terra::rast(bin_0to2_percent_paths[ids_bin_0to2 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_2to5_raster <- terra::rast(bin_2to5_percent_paths[ids_bin_2to5 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_5to10_raster <- terra::rast(bin_5to10_percent_paths[ids_bin_5to10 == single_tile_id][1])
    bin_10plus_raster <- terra::rast(bin_10plus_percent_paths[ids_bin_10plus == single_tile_id][1])

    stacked_bin_percent_rasters <- c(
      bin_0to2_raster,
      bin_2to5_raster,
      bin_5to10_raster,
      bin_10plus_raster
    )

    fhd_raster <- terra::app(
      stacked_bin_percent_rasters,
      fun = safe_fhd_function
    )

    safe_write_raster(
      fhd_raster,
      file.path(output_folder_path, paste0(single_tile_id, "_fhd_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}

compute_fhd_from_vertical_bin_percent_rasters(utm11_dirs$vertical_bins_5m, utm11_dirs$fhd_res5m)
compute_fhd_from_vertical_bin_percent_rasters(utm12_dirs$vertical_bins_5m, utm12_dirs$fhd_res5m)


##### Compute Gap Fraction From Cover #####
# gap fraction = 1 - cover which is derived from the cover rasters already written above

compute_gap_fraction_from_cover_folder <- function(summary_folder_path, output_folder_path) {

  cover_file_paths <- list.files(
    summary_folder_path,
    pattern = "_cover_5m\\.tif$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(length(cover_file_paths) > 0)

  for (single_cover_file_path in cover_file_paths) {

    cover_raster <- terra::rast(single_cover_file_path)
    gap_fraction_raster <- 1 - cover_raster

    cover_base_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_cover_file_path))
    gap_base_name <- sub("_cover_5m$", "", cover_base_name)

    safe_write_raster(
      gap_fraction_raster,
      file.path(output_folder_path, paste0(gap_base_name, "_gapfrac_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}

compute_gap_fraction_from_cover_folder(
  utm11_dirs$vertical_bins_5m$summary,
  utm11_dirs$gap_fraction_res5m
)

compute_gap_fraction_from_cover_folder(
  utm12_dirs$vertical_bins_5m$summary,
  utm12_dirs$gap_fraction_res5m
)


##### Compute Rugosity From CHM #####
# - Rugosity here = SD of 1m CHM heights aggregated to 5m and represents the canopy-surface roughness metric

compute_rugosity_from_chm_folder <- function(chm_folder_path, rugosity_folder_path) {

  chm_file_paths <- list.files(
    chm_folder_path,
    pattern = "_chm\\.(tif|grd)$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(length(chm_file_paths) > 0)

  for (single_chm_file_path in chm_file_paths) {

    chm_raster_1m <- terra::rast(single_chm_file_path)

    rugosity_sd_raster_5m <- terra::aggregate(
      chm_raster_1m,
      fact = 5,
      fun = sd,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    chm_base_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_chm_file_path))

    safe_write_raster(
      rugosity_sd_raster_5m,
      file.path(rugosity_folder_path, paste0(chm_base_name, "_rugosity_sd_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}

compute_rugosity_from_chm_folder(utm11_dirs$chm_res1m, utm11_dirs$rugosity_res5m)
compute_rugosity_from_chm_folder(utm12_dirs$chm_res1m, utm12_dirs$rugosity_res5m)


##### Compute Rumple From CHM #####
# Rumple index is surface area / planar area
# We approximate canopy surface area from local CHM slope and then aggregate to 5m
# NOTE:
# This is CHM-based rumple, not point-cloud rumple which is usually the more standard interpretation for this metric

compute_rumple_from_chm_folder <- function(chm_folder_path, rumple_folder_path) {

  chm_file_paths <- list.files(
    chm_folder_path,
    pattern = "_chm\\.(tif|grd)$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  stopifnot(length(chm_file_paths) > 0)

  for (single_chm_file_path in chm_file_paths) {

    chm_raster_1m <- terra::rast(single_chm_file_path)

    chm_slope_radians <- terra::terrain(
      chm_raster_1m,
      v = "slope",
      unit = "radians",
      neighbors = 8
    )

    cell_resolution <- terra::res(chm_raster_1m)
    planar_cell_area_m2 <- cell_resolution[1] * cell_resolution[2]

    # Surface area approximation for each CHM cell
    surface_area_raster_1m <- planar_cell_area_m2 / cos(chm_slope_radians)

    # Aggregate summed surface area into 5m cells
    surface_area_sum_raster_5m <- terra::aggregate(
      surface_area_raster_1m,
      fact = 5,
      fun = sum,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    planar_area_raster_5m <- surface_area_sum_raster_5m
    terra::values(planar_area_raster_5m) <- planar_cell_area_m2 * 25

    rumple_index_raster_5m <- surface_area_sum_raster_5m / planar_area_raster_5m

    chm_base_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_chm_file_path))

    safe_write_raster(
      rumple_index_raster_5m,
      file.path(rumple_folder_path, paste0(chm_base_name, "_rumple_5m.tif"))
    )
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}

compute_rumple_from_chm_folder(utm11_dirs$chm_res1m, utm11_dirs$rumple_res5m)
compute_rumple_from_chm_folder(utm12_dirs$chm_res1m, utm12_dirs$rumple_res5m)


##### Compute Complexity From Point Cloud At 5m #####
# Complexity here is a point-cloud structural variability metric:
# sd(Z) / mean(Z) for vegetation points in each 5m cell

compute_point_cloud_complexity_raster <- function(cluster, ...) {

  normalized_las_object <- lidR::readLAS(cluster)

  if (lidR::is.empty(normalized_las_object)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  vegetation_points_las <- lidR::filter_poi(
    normalized_las_object,
    Classification != 2L & Z > 0
  )

  if (lidR::is.empty(vegetation_points_las)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  complexity_raster_1m <- lidR::pixel_metrics(
    vegetation_points_las,
    ~safe_complexity_function(Z),
    res = 1
  )

  complexity_raster_1m
}

lidR::opt_output_files(ctg_norm_utm11) <- file.path(
  utm11_dirs$complexity_res1m,
  "{ORIGINALFILENAME}_complexity_1m"
)

lidR::catalog_apply(ctg_norm_utm11, compute_point_cloud_complexity_raster)

lidR::opt_output_files(ctg_norm_utm12) <- file.path(
  utm12_dirs$complexity_res1m,
  "{ORIGINALFILENAME}_complexity_1m"
)

lidR::catalog_apply(ctg_norm_utm12, compute_point_cloud_complexity_raster)

cat("All UTM12 outputs saved under: ", metrics_utm12_root_dir, "\n")

print(utm11_dirs)

We can use the *future* package to parallel process the liDAR data and try to work through the pipeline faster. We will start by setting up this process and creating a place to save temp files. Temp files are a just-in-case measure since most of the data is connecting to a network. I will be saving the fully processed tiles in the network drive in case we have to access them later from a different computer.

Next we want to direct R to where our files live. As a note, each folder is the entire laz dataset for a single flight. File names are not consistent so we will have to tell R to take any LAZ file from within our network drive (R:/). Our shapefile for our study area is also found in this network drive and we will want to load it in because we only want to spend time on tiles that intersect our study area.

## Index Tiles in Study Area and Store as a Backup

We want to read in the study area shapefile then repair any invalid geometry (if needed). We can then read in the tile keys and separate them out by South Hills and Albion as they'll need to be handled individually due to the CRS of the LAZ files.

##### Build Helper Function To Read Tile Index Shapefile #####

# The purpose of this helper function is to read one tile index shapefile, add metadata about which flight it came from, and return a consistent sf object.

read_tile_index_with_metadata <- function(single_tile_index_path) {

  # Read the tile index
  single_tile_index_sf <- st_read(single_tile_index_path, quiet = TRUE)

  # Repair geometry if needed
  single_tile_index_sf <- st_make_valid(single_tile_index_sf)

  # Add the source shapefile name so we always know which flight this came from
  single_tile_index_sf$tile_index_source_file <- basename(single_tile_index_path)

  # Add a simpler flight label based on the shapefile file name
  single_tile_index_sf$flight_name <- file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_tile_index_path))

  single_tile_index_sf
}


##### Read All Tile Index Shapefiles #####

# Read every tile index shapefile and keep them in a list first
tile_index_sf_list <- lapply(
  tile_index_shapefile_paths,
  read_tile_index_with_metadata
)

# Name the list elements for readability
names(tile_index_sf_list) <- file_path_sans_ext(basename(tile_index_shapefile_paths))

# Quick preview of what was read
print(names(tile_index_sf_list))


##### Inspect Tile Index Attribute Names #####

  cat("\n====================\n")
  cat("Tile index:", single_name, "\n")
  cat("====================\n")
  print(names(tile_index_sf_list[[single_name]]))
}

# After running this block, we need to identify the field in the tile index that stores
# the spatial tile code. Here we need to use Tilename

##### Define Tile Code Field #####

# Tell R where the Tile Code is found
tile_code_field_name <- "Tilename"

# Verify that every tile index contains this field
tile_code_field_missing <- vapply(
  tile_index_sf_list,
  function(single_sf) !(tile_code_field_name %in% names(single_sf)),
  logical(1)
)

if (any(tile_code_field_missing)) {
  stop(
    "The tile code field '", tile_code_field_name,
    "' was not found in these tile index shapefiles:\n",
    paste(names(tile_index_sf_list)[tile_code_field_missing], collapse = "\n")
  )
}

##### Standardize Tile Index Attribute Tables #####

# Here we will convert each tile index to a standard schema:
# - flight_name
# - tile_index_source_file
# - tile_code
# - geometry
#
# This makes later joining and counting much easier.

standardized_tile_index_sf_list <- lapply(tile_index_sf_list, function(single_sf) {

  # Copy the source field into a clean common field name
  single_sf$tile_code <- as.character(single_sf[[tile_code_field_name]])

  # Remove whitespace just in case
  single_sf$tile_code <- trimws(single_sf$tile_code)

  single_sf[, c("flight_name", "tile_index_source_file", "tile_code", attr(single_sf, "sf_column"))]
})

##### Preview Standardized Tile Index Layers #####

# Because the tile indexes are in different CRS, we will want to preview them one at a time.

for (single_name in names(standardized_tile_index_sf_list)) {

  cat("\n====================\n")
  cat("Standardized tile index:", single_name, "\n")
  cat("====================\n")

  print(
    standardized_tile_index_sf_list[[single_name]][
      1:min(5, nrow(standardized_tile_index_sf_list[[single_name]])),
    ]
  )
}

##### Intersect Tile Index With South Hills ROI #####

# We transform the ROI into the CRS of each tile index before intersecting.
# Since each shapefile may have its own CRS, we do the selection flight-by-flight.

southhills_selected_list <- lapply(standardized_tile_index_sf_list, function(single_tile_index_sf) {

  # Transform South Hills ROI into the CRS used by this tile index
  southhills_roi_in_tile_crs <- st_transform(
    southhills_roi_sf,
    st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)
  )

  # Keep only the intersecting tiles
  selected_sf <- single_tile_index_sf[
    lengths(st_intersects(single_tile_index_sf, southhills_roi_in_tile_crs)) > 0,
  ]

  # If this flight contributes no South Hills tiles, return NULL
  if (nrow(selected_sf) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Add study area label
  selected_sf$study_area_name <- rep("SouthHills", nrow(selected_sf))

  # Add CRS metadata for later processing-group definition
  selected_sf$crs_name <- rep(st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)$Name, nrow(selected_sf))
  selected_sf$crs_epsg <- rep(st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)$epsg, nrow(selected_sf))

  selected_sf
})


##### Intersect Tile Index With Albion ROI #####

# Same logic as above, but for Albion

albion_selected_list <- lapply(standardized_tile_index_sf_list, function(single_tile_index_sf) {

  # Transform Albion ROI into the CRS used by this tile index
  albion_roi_in_tile_crs <- st_transform(
    albion_roi_sf,
    st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)
  )

  # Keep only the intersecting tiles
  selected_sf <- single_tile_index_sf[
    lengths(st_intersects(single_tile_index_sf, albion_roi_in_tile_crs)) > 0,
  ]

  # If this flight contributes no Albion tiles, return NULL
  if (nrow(selected_sf) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Add study area label
  selected_sf$study_area_name <- rep("Albion", nrow(selected_sf))

  # Add CRS metadata for later processing-group definition
  selected_sf$crs_name <- rep(st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)$Name, nrow(selected_sf))
  selected_sf$crs_epsg <- rep(st_crs(single_tile_index_sf)$epsg, nrow(selected_sf))

  selected_sf
})

##### Remove NULL Entries #####

southhills_selected_list <- southhills_selected_list[!vapply(southhills_selected_list, is.null, logical(1))]
albion_selected_list     <- albion_selected_list[!vapply(albion_selected_list, is.null, logical(1))]

albion_selected_tiles_table <- rbindlist(

# Read the contents of each Zip file without extracting it
# Creates a table of archived file name that we can match against tile code

zip_inventory_list <- lapply(downloaded_zip_file_paths, function(single_zip_path) {

  # List the archive contents without extracting
  single_zip_contents <- utils::unzip(single_zip_path, list = TRUE)

  # If archive is empty or unreadable, return a minimal placeholder record
  if (is.null(single_zip_contents) || nrow(single_zip_contents) == 0) {
    return(data.table(
      zip_file_path = single_zip_path,
      zip_file_name = basename(single_zip_path),
      archived_file_name = NA_character_,
      archived_file_size = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  # Otherwise build one row per archived file
  data.table(
    zip_file_path      = single_zip_path,
    zip_file_name      = basename(single_zip_path),
    archived_file_name = single_zip_contents$Name,
    archived_file_size = single_zip_contents$Length
  )
})

zip_inventory_table <- rbindlist(zip_inventory_list, fill = TRUE)

# Keep only LAS/LAZ files listed inside ZIPs

  grepl("\\.(las|laz)$", archived_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE)

# For each selected tile in the locked manifest, find archived LAZ/LAS file names that contain that tile code.

matched_tile_rows_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(selected_tile_manifest_table)), function(i) {

  single_tile_code        <- selected_tile_manifest_table$tile_code[i]
  single_flight_name      <- selected_tile_manifest_table$flight_name[i]
  single_study_area       <- selected_tile_manifest_table$study_area_name[i]
  single_processing_group <- selected_tile_manifest_table$processing_group[i]
  single_raw_dir          <- selected_tile_manifest_table$study_area_raw_directory[i]

  # Find archive entries whose file name contains this tile code
  candidate_matches <- zip_inventory_lidar_table[
    grepl(single_tile_code, archived_file_name, fixed = TRUE)
  ]

  # Add manifest metadata to the matching rows
  if (nrow(candidate_matches) > 0) {

    # Copy so we do not accidentally modify the source table by reference
    candidate_matches <- copy(candidate_matches)

    candidate_matches[, tile_code := single_tile_code]
    candidate_matches[, flight_name := single_flight_name]
    candidate_matches[, study_area_name := single_study_area]
    candidate_matches[, processing_group := single_processing_group]
    candidate_matches[, target_raw_directory := single_raw_dir]

  } else {

    # If there were no matches, return one placeholder row so the tile is still tracked
    candidate_matches <- data.table(
      zip_file_path = NA_character_,
      zip_file_name = NA_character_,
      archived_file_name = NA_character_,
      archived_file_size = NA_real_,
      tile_code = single_tile_code,
      flight_name = single_flight_name,
      study_area_name = single_study_area,
      processing_group = single_processing_group,
      target_raw_directory = single_raw_dir
    )
  }

  candidate_matches
})

matched_tiles_table <- rbindlist(matched_tile_rows_list, fill = TRUE)

]

# 1. Matches between Elko and SouthernID_2018_12 we want to keep Elko tiles as this one was more recent and would capture images post 2020 Badger Fire.

##### Define Backup Folder For All Matched Candidate Tiles #####
# Create a durable folder that will store ALL matched candidate LAS/LAZ tiles from the ZIP archives, including duplicates / overlaps.
# IMPORTANT:
# This is a BACKUP / RECOVERY folder, not the final cleaned tile set. We are intentionally preserving all matched candidates here.

all_matched_candidate_backup_directory <- file.path(
  "G:/01_raw_tiles_selected",
  "All_Matched_Candidate_Tiles_Backup"
)

dir.create(
  all_matched_candidate_backup_directory,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


##### Build Extraction Table For Real Archive Matches Only #####
# Keep only rows where we actually found a LAS/LAZ file inside a ZIP archive.
# Placeholder rows with NA archive names are not extractable and should be excluded.

matched_tiles_extractable_table <- matched_tiles_table[
  !is.na(zip_file_path) &
  !is.na(archived_file_name)
]

cat("Matched rows with extractable archive files:", nrow(matched_tiles_extractable_table), "\n")


##### Remove Exact Duplicate ZIP + Archived File Pairs #####
# The same archived LAS/LAZ file could appear more than once in matched_tiles_table if the same tile code was represented multiple times in the manifest logic.
# We only want to extract each physical archived file ONCE into the backup folder.
# This still preserves all unique candidate files, but avoids extracting the exact same ZIP member multiple times.

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table <- matched_tiles_extractable_table[
  !duplicated(paste(zip_file_path, archived_file_name, sep = " || "))
]

cat(
  "Unique archived LAS/LAZ files to extract for backup:",
  nrow(matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table),
  "\n"
)


##### Build Safe Output File Names #####
# Archived file names may repeat across ZIPs or flights.
# To prevent overwrite, we create a stable backup file name that includes:
# - flight name
# - tile code
# - source ZIP name
# - original archived base file name
#
# This makes the backup folder much safer and easier to audit later.

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  zip_name_no_ext := tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(zip_file_name))
]

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  archived_base_name := basename(archived_file_name)
]

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  backup_output_file_name := paste(
    flight_name,
    tile_code,
    zip_name_no_ext,
    archived_base_name,
    sep = "__"
  )
]

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  backup_output_file_path := file.path(
    all_matched_candidate_backup_directory,
    backup_output_file_name
  )
]


##### QA Check For Duplicate Backup Output Names #####
# Confirm our naming scheme does not accidentally create collisions. If collisions exist, we should stop now rather than overwrite files.

duplicate_backup_names_table <- matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  .N,
  by = backup_output_file_name
][N > 1]

if (nrow(duplicate_backup_names_table) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Duplicate backup output names were generated. ",
    "Review naming logic before extraction."
  )
}

cat("Backup output naming QA passed. No output name collisions found.\n")


##### Save Backup Extraction Manifest Before Running #####
# Save a record of exactly what we intend to extract before extraction begins.This makes the backup step reproducible.

fwrite(
  matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table,
  file.path(project_root_directory, "04_logs", "matched_tiles_backup_extraction_manifest.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table,
  file.path(project_root_directory, "04_logs", "matched_tiles_backup_extraction_manifest.rds")
)


##### Extract All Matched Candidate Tiles From ZIP Archives #####
# Extract each matched LAS/LAZ file from its ZIP archive into the backup folder.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - We extract one archived file at a time
# - We rename it immediately to the safe backup name
# - If the file already exists, we skip it
# - We write a detailed extraction log for troubleshooting

backup_extraction_log_path <- file.path(
  project_root_directory,
  "04_logs",
  "matched_tiles_backup_extraction_log.txt"
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table))) {

  single_zip_file_path <- matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table$zip_file_path[i]
  single_archived_file_name <- matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table$archived_file_name[i]
  single_backup_output_file_path <- matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table$backup_output_file_path[i]

  cat(
    "Processing backup extraction", i, "of",
    nrow(matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table), "\n"
  )

  # Skip if this backup file already exists
  if (file.exists(single_backup_output_file_path)) {

    cat(
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
      " - SKIP already exists - ",
      single_backup_output_file_path,
      "\n",
      sep = "",
      file = backup_extraction_log_path,
      append = TRUE
    )

    next
  }

  # Temporary extraction folder
  single_temp_extract_directory <- file.path(
    project_root_directory,
    "temp",
    "zip_extract_temp"
  )

  dir.create(
    single_temp_extract_directory,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )

  # Try extraction
  tryCatch({

    # Extract only the one archived LAS/LAZ file we want from the ZIP
    extracted_file_path <- utils::unzip(
      zipfile = single_zip_file_path,
      files = single_archived_file_name,
      exdir = single_temp_extract_directory,
      overwrite = TRUE
    )

    # unzip() returns the extracted path(s); confirm something was returned
    if (length(extracted_file_path) == 0 || !file.exists(extracted_file_path[1])) {
      stop("Extraction returned no readable file.")
    }

    # Move extracted file into the backup folder using the safe name
    file.rename(
      from = extracted_file_path[1],
      to   = single_backup_output_file_path
    )

    # Confirm final file exists
    if (!file.exists(single_backup_output_file_path)) {
      stop("File move to backup folder failed.")
    }

    cat(
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
      " - EXTRACTED - ZIP: ",
      single_zip_file_path,
      " | ARCHIVED: ",
      single_archived_file_name,
      " | OUTPUT: ",
      single_backup_output_file_path,
      "\n",
      sep = "",
      file = backup_extraction_log_path,
      append = TRUE
    )

  }, error = function(e) {

    cat(
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
      " - ERROR - ZIP: ",
      single_zip_file_path,
      " | ARCHIVED: ",
      single_archived_file_name,
      " | MESSAGE: ",
      conditionMessage(e),
      "\n",
      sep = "",
      file = backup_extraction_log_path,
      append = TRUE
    )
  })
}


##### Build Post-Extraction QA Table #####

# PURPOSE:
# Check which intended backup files now exist on disk after extraction.

matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  backup_file_exists := file.exists(backup_output_file_path)
]

backup_extraction_summary_table <- matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table[
  ,
  .(
    n_expected_backup_files = .N,
    n_existing_backup_files = sum(backup_file_exists),
    n_missing_backup_files  = sum(!backup_file_exists)
  )
]

print(backup_extraction_summary_table)

fwrite(
  matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table,
  file.path(project_root_directory, "04_logs", "matched_tiles_backup_extraction_results.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  matched_tiles_extractable_unique_table,
  file.path(project_root_directory, "04_logs", "matched_tiles_backup_extraction_results.rds")
)

cat(
  "\nBackup extraction complete.\n",
  "Backup folder: ", all_matched_candidate_backup_directory, "\n",
  "Expected backup files: ", backup_extraction_summary_table$n_expected_backup_files, "\n",
  "Existing backup files: ", backup_extraction_summary_table$n_existing_backup_files, "\n",
  "Missing backup files : ", backup_extraction_summary_table$n_missing_backup_files, "\n",
  sep = ""
)

```

Okay with our tiles within our study area identified and backed up. We can continue with our pipeline.

## Load Study Area

We want to load the study area and have R identify which tiles overlap it. Even though we have done something similar with the QGIS and our matched tiles, that was only using the tile code names. This will use the spatial extent of the tiles. First, we will want to verify that the shapefile and LAZ/LAS files are in the same CRS otherwise this whole thing will fail.

```{r Verify CRS}
# CRS of the shapefile should be EPSG: 8826 but let's confirm
study_area   <- st_read(study_area_shapefile_path, quiet = TRUE)
study_area   <- st_make_valid(study_area)

# Ensure we have explicit polygon rows (so [2,] really means boundary 2)
study_area_polygon_rows <- st_cast(study_area, "POLYGON", warn = FALSE)

st_crs(study_area)

# Try to find LAZ CRS
h1 <- lidR::readLASheader(tile_files[1])
las_has_crs <- FALSE
try({
     crs_guess <- lidR::st_crs(h1)
     if (!is.na(crs_guess)) {
         print(crs_guess)
         las_has_crs <- TRUE
     }
 }, silent = TRUE)

# 1) Pick a representative LAZ from your dataset (any one is fine)
one_tile <- tile_files[1]

# 2) Read CRS from LAZ header
h1 <- lidR::readLASheader(one_tile)
crs_lidar <- lidR::st_crs(h1)   # you already proved this works

crs_lidar  # print it

# Transform study area to match LAZ
if (is.na(st_crs(study_area))) stop("Study shapefile CRS is NA in R (undefined). Fix it before transforming.")

study_area <- st_transform(study_area, crs_lidar)
st_crs(study_area) == st_crs(h1) #asks true or false if they match
```

## Find Only Tiles in Study Area

We do not want to process the entire dataset. We ONLY want those that fall within our study area, so we are going to use the st_intersection function to find only tiles in our study area. Instead of loading in every point cloud or cataloging all of the tiles, we are going to create a table that lists the bounding box of each LAZ/LAS file and use that to find which overlap.

```{r Find the Tiles!}
# Build a footprint (bbox polygon) for every LAZ/LAS using the header
study_union <- st_union(study_area)

# --- single pass header read (with tryCatch) ---
tile_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(tile_files, function(f) {
  tryCatch({
    h <- lidR::readLASheader(f)
    data.table(
      file = f,
      ok   = TRUE,
      xmin = h@PHB[["Min X"]],
      xmax = h@PHB[["Max X"]],
      ymin = h@PHB[["Min Y"]],
      ymax = h@PHB[["Max Y"]]
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    data.table(file = f, ok = FALSE)
  })
}), fill = TRUE)

# --- sanity: header failures ---
sum(!tile_dt$ok)
# Save immediately so you don’t redo this step
saveRDS(tile_dt, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/tile_dt_headers.rds")

# --- sanity: bad extents ---
bad_extent <- tile_dt[ok == TRUE & (xmax <= xmin | ymax <= ymin | is.na(xmin) | is.na(ymin))]
nrow(bad_extent)
# Optional: save a list of problematic files
if (nrow(bad_extent) > 0) {
  writeLines(bad_extent$file, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/bad_extent_files.txt")
}

# --- build polygons only for good headers ---
tile_ok <- tile_dt[ok == TRUE]

tile_sf <- st_as_sf(tile_ok, coords = c("xmin","ymin"), crs = crs_lidar) # dummy
tile_sf$geometry <- st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tile_ok)), function(i) {
  st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymin[i],
      tile_ok$xmax[i], tile_ok$ymin[i],
      tile_ok$xmax[i], tile_ok$ymax[i],
      tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymax[i],
      tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymin[i]),
    ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
  )))
}), crs = crs_lidar)

# --- sanity: CRS match ---
stopifnot(st_crs(tile_sf) == st_crs(study_union))

# --- intersects ---
hits <- st_intersects(tile_sf, study_union, sparse = FALSE)[, 1]
keep_files <- tile_sf$file[hits]

length(tile_files)
length(keep_files)

# Save keep list for tomorrow
saveRDS(keep_files, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/keep_files.rds")
writeLines(keep_files, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/keep_files.txt")
```

# Read in kept tiles

# Catalog from selected tiles

## Set up Filter
# One output per input tile
opt_chunk_size(ctg_filter_AOI)   <- 0
opt_chunk_buffer(ctg_filter_AOI) <- 0

# Parallel + stability
options(lidR.cores = 8)
lidR::set_lidr_threads(1)

# Output folders (on R:)
run_root <- "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR"
out_filtered <- file.path(run_root, "01_filtered")
log_dir <- file.path(run_root, "04_logs")
dir.create(out_filtered, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(log_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Unique naming (prevents collisions across flights)
opt_output_files(ctg_filter_AOI) <- file.path(out_filtered, "{ORIGINALFILENAME}_{ID}_filtered")

# Filter function (won't crash the whole run if 1 tile fails)
filter_fun_AOI <- function(x, ...) {
  tryCatch({
    if (inherits(x, "LAScluster")) x <- readLAS(x)
    if (is.null(x) || is.empty(x)) return(NULL)

    x <- filter_poi(x, !Withheld_flag & !Synthetic_flag)
    x <- classify_noise(x, ivf(res = 4, n = 12))
    x <- filter_poi(x, !Classification %in% c(7L, 18L))

    if (is.empty(x)) return(NULL)
    x
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(Sys.time(), "- ERROR:", conditionMessage(e), "\n",
        file = file.path(log_dir, "filter_errors.txt"),
        append = TRUE)
    NULL
  })
}

# Run (you'll see the lidR progress bar)
Filter_AOI <- catalog_apply(ctg_filter_AOI, filter_fun_AOI)
Filter_AOI
