### Debug Albion Missing Tiles

We can see the albion tiles weren't captured in our earlier extraction. We need to figure out the reason and get the albion tiles back in the pipeline.

Files were not captured due to differences in CRS between flights that covered the South Hills and the Ablions. Best course of action is to keep them in separate CRS throughout the pipeline (run them and save them separatly). We will keep the file directory for the South Hills, create a new one for the albions, filter the Albions, and continue down the pipeline.

**After metric rasters area created, we will reproject them into the same CRS.**

```{r Debug missing tiles}
############# STEP: LiDAR Inventory + CRS Audit (HEADER ONLY) ############
## Purpose:
##   1) Confirm ALL flights share ONE CRS (or detect multiple)
##   2) Confirm we have tile coverage candidates near Study Area 2
##   3) Produce saved audit tables for reproducibility
##
## This does NOT re-filter or write any LAS outputs.

######### 0) Define durable paths ###########

pipeline_log_directory      <- file.path("R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs")
dir.create(pipeline_log_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

####### 1) Full tile inventory (do not overwrite generic names) ######

lidar_all_tile_paths_full_inventory <- tile_files  # your existing discovered list

if (length(lidar_all_tile_paths_full_inventory) == 0) {
  stop("lidar_all_tile_paths_full_inventory is empty. Tile discovery failed.")
}

######### 2) Read Study Area shapefile while preserving polygon rows #########
##    DO NOT st_union() this object; we need Albion Section explicitly.

study_area_features_raw   <- st_read(study_area_shapefile_path, quiet = TRUE)
study_area_features_raw   <- st_make_valid(study_area_features_raw)

# Ensure we have explicit polygon rows (so [2,] really means boundary 2)
study_area_polygon_rows <- st_cast(study_area_features_raw, "POLYGON", warn = FALSE)

# Prefer attribute-based selection for reproducibility
study_area_polygon_albion <- study_area_polygon_rows[study_area_polygon_rows$Section == "Albion", ]
if (nrow(study_area_polygon_albion) != 1) stop("Albion selection did not return.")

study_area_polygon_albion <- study_area_polygon_rows[study_area_polygon_rows$Section == "Albion", ]

######### 3) Build header inventory table INCLUDING CRS per tile ###########
##    This detects multi-CRS issues across flights.

lidar_header_inventory_table <- rbindlist(lapply(lidar_all_tile_paths_full_inventory, function(single_tile_path) {
  tryCatch({
    tile_header_object <- lidR::readLASheader(single_tile_path)

    # Extract extents
    tile_xmin <- tile_header_object@PHB[["Min X"]]
    tile_xmax <- tile_header_object@PHB[["Max X"]]
    tile_ymin <- tile_header_object@PHB[["Min Y"]]
    tile_ymax <- tile_header_object@PHB[["Max Y"]]

    # CRS from header (may be NA)
    tile_crs_object <- tryCatch(lidR::st_crs(tile_header_object), error = function(e) NA)

    data.table(
      tile_path          = single_tile_path,
      header_read_ok     = TRUE,
      xmin               = tile_xmin,
      xmax               = tile_xmax,
      ymin               = tile_ymin,
      ymax               = tile_ymax,
      crs_epsg           = if (is.na(tile_crs_object)) NA_integer_ else tile_crs_object$epsg,
      crs_wkt            = if (is.na(tile_crs_object)) NA_character_ else tile_crs_object$wkt,
      flight_folder_name = sub("^R:/([^/]+)/.*", "\\1", single_tile_path)
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    data.table(
      tile_path          = single_tile_path,
      header_read_ok     = FALSE,
      xmin               = NA_real_,
      xmax               = NA_real_,
      ymin               = NA_real_,
      ymax               = NA_real_,
      crs_epsg           = NA_integer_,
      crs_wkt            = NA_character_,
      flight_folder_name = sub("^R:/([^/]+)/.*", "\\1", single_tile_path)
    )
  })
}), fill = TRUE)

## Save inventory for reproducibility (you never have to re-run header reads)
saveRDS(
  lidar_header_inventory_table,
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "lidar_header_inventory_full.rds")
)

cat("Header read failures:", sum(!lidar_header_inventory_table$header_read_ok), "\n")

###### 4) Flight tile counts (informational; helps spot missing flights) ##########

lidar_tiles_per_flight_folder_table <- lidar_header_inventory_table[
  , .(tile_count = .N,
      header_failures = sum(!header_read_ok)),
  by = flight_folder_name
][order(-tile_count)]

print(lidar_tiles_per_flight_folder_table)

saveRDS(
  lidar_tiles_per_flight_folder_table,
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "lidar_tiles_per_flight_folder_table.rds")
)

##### 5) CRS audit: hard stop if multiple CRSs present among readable tiles ##########

lidar_readable_tiles_table <- lidar_header_inventory_table[header_read_ok == TRUE]

unique_crs_wkt_values <- unique(na.omit(lidar_readable_tiles_table$crs_wkt))

cat("Distinct CRS (WKT) among readable tiles:", length(unique_crs_wkt_values), "\n")

if (length(unique_crs_wkt_values) == 0) {
  stop("No readable CRS info found in headers. CRS is missing from tiles; cannot guarantee alignment.")
}

if (length(unique_crs_wkt_values) > 1) {
  # Show which flights have which CRS
  crs_by_flight_table <- lidar_readable_tiles_table[
    , .(n_tiles = .N),
    by = .(flight_folder_name, crs_epsg)
  ][order(flight_folder_name, crs_epsg)]

  print(crs_by_flight_table)

  saveRDS(
    crs_by_flight_table,
    file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "crs_by_flight_table.rds")
  )

  stop("MULTIPLE LiDAR CRSs detected across flights. Do NOT mix these in one pipeline run. Split by CRS or reproject.")
}

# See 3 different CRS used

# Input: lidar_header_inventory_table already exists in your session
# Output: lidar_crs_group_by_flight_table + saved RDS

lidar_readable_tiles_table <- lidar_header_inventory_table[header_read_ok == TRUE]

# Create a stable CRS "group id" based on WKT text.
# (We use a short hash-like id derived from the first 60 chars + nchar for readability.)
lidar_readable_tiles_table[, crs_wkt_prefix := substr(crs_wkt, 1, 60)]
lidar_readable_tiles_table[, crs_wkt_length := nchar(crs_wkt)]

lidar_crs_group_by_flight_table <- lidar_readable_tiles_table[
  , .(n_tiles = .N),
  by = .(flight_folder_name, crs_wkt_prefix, crs_wkt_length)
][order(flight_folder_name, -n_tiles)]

print(lidar_crs_group_by_flight_table)

saveRDS(
  lidar_crs_group_by_flight_table,
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "lidar_crs_group_by_flight_table.rds")
)

##   - Identify which of the 3 CRS WKT strings equals the target CRS

target_lidar_crs_object <- crs_lidar  # reuse your already-defined target CRS object
target_wkt_string       <- target_lidar_crs_object$wkt

lidar_distinct_crs_table <- data.table(
  crs_wkt = unique(na.omit(lidar_readable_tiles_table$crs_wkt))
)

lidar_distinct_crs_table[, wkt_equals_target := (crs_wkt == target_wkt_string)]
lidar_distinct_crs_table[, crs_wkt_prefix := substr(crs_wkt, 1, 80)]
lidar_distinct_crs_table[, crs_wkt_length := nchar(crs_wkt)]

print(lidar_distinct_crs_table[, .(wkt_equals_target, crs_wkt_prefix, crs_wkt_length)])

# Same as your target CRS (UTM zone 11N + NAVD88 height Geoid12B) ✅

# 07_Cassia — 142 tiles
# Part21 — 313 tiles
# Part22 — 472 tiles
# ElkoNW_LAZ — mostly target CRS, but mixed (see below)

# Different CRS (UTM zone 12N + NAVD88 height Geoid12B) ❌

# LAZ — 5,449 tiles (zone 12N)
# SouthernIdaho2018_14_LAZ — 3,299 tiles (zone 12N)

saveRDS(lidar_distinct_crs_table, file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "lidar_distinct_crs_table.rds"))

## COORDINATE RANGE CHECK BY CRS GROUP (SAFE)
## Purpose: 1) Detect whether CRS groups are truly in different coordinate spaces and 2) If ranges overlap tightly, differences may be metadata-only

coordinate_ranges_by_crs_table <- lidar_readable_tiles_table[
  , .(
    xmin_min = min(xmin, na.rm = TRUE),
    xmax_max = max(xmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymin_min = min(ymin, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymax_max = max(ymax, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tiles  = .N
  ),
  by = .(crs_wkt_prefix, crs_wkt_length)
][order(-n_tiles)]

print(coordinate_ranges_by_crs_table)
saveRDS(coordinate_ranges_by_crs_table, file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "coordinate_ranges_by_crs_table.rds"))

##### STEP 6: Albion coverage audit by CRS group (HEADER ONLY) ########
## Purpose:
##   - Identify which CRS group(s) contain tiles near Albion
##   - Avoid reprojecting or processing unnecessary tiles
##   - Save candidate lists to logs for reproducibility
##
## Outputs:
##   - logs/albion_tile_candidates_header_only.rds
##   - logs/albion_tile_candidates_summary_by_crs_group.rds

# Create a stable CRS group label for each tile (explicit, human-readable)
albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table <- data.table::copy(lidar_readable_tiles_table)

albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table[, crs_group_label := data.table::fifelse(
  grepl("UTM zone 12N", crs_wkt, fixed = TRUE), "utm12_geoid12B",
  data.table::fifelse(
    grepl("Geoid18", crs_wkt, fixed = TRUE), "utm11_geoid18",
    "utm11_geoid12B_target"
  )
)]

# We will bbox-filter Albion separately within each CRS group
albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table[, is_within_albion_bbox_in_that_crs := FALSE]

# Loop CRS groups to transform Albion polygon into each group CRS and do a fast bbox overlap test
for (single_crs_group_label in unique(albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table$crs_group_label)) {

  # Pull one example WKT to define the CRS object for this group
  example_wkt_for_group <- albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table[
    crs_group_label == single_crs_group_label, crs_wkt
  ][1]

  crs_object_for_group <- sf::st_crs(example_wkt_for_group)

  # Transform Albion polygon into this CRS group for apples-to-apples bbox comparison
  albion_polygon_in_group_crs <- sf::st_transform(study_area_polygon_albion, crs_object_for_group)
  albion_bbox_in_group_crs    <- sf::st_bbox(albion_polygon_in_group_crs)

  # Flag tiles in this CRS group whose header bbox overlaps Albion bbox
  albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table[
    crs_group_label == single_crs_group_label &
      !(
        xmax < albion_bbox_in_group_crs["xmin"] |
        xmin > albion_bbox_in_group_crs["xmax"] |
        ymax < albion_bbox_in_group_crs["ymin"] |
        ymin > albion_bbox_in_group_crs["ymax"]
      ),
    is_within_albion_bbox_in_that_crs := TRUE
  ]
}

# Subset to just Albion bbox candidates (still header-only)
albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table <- albion_tile_candidate_inventory_table[
  is_within_albion_bbox_in_that_crs == TRUE
]

# Summarize: where is Albion coverage likely coming from?
albion_tile_candidates_summary_by_crs_group <- albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table[
  , .(n_candidate_tiles = .N),
  by = .(crs_group_label, flight_folder_name)
][order(crs_group_label, -n_candidate_tiles)]

print(albion_tile_candidates_summary_by_crs_group)

# Save for reproducibility
saveRDS(
  albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table,
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "albion_tile_candidates_header_only.rds")
)

saveRDS(
  albion_tile_candidates_summary_by_crs_group,
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "albion_tile_candidates_summary_by_crs_group.rds")
)

###### STEP 7: Build TRUE intersecting Albion keep lists (HEADER ONLY) ##########
## Purpose:
##   - Convert candidate tile header bboxes to footprint polygons
##   - Perform true intersection with Albion (in each CRS group)
##   - Save definitive keep lists per CRS group
##
## Outputs:
##   - logs/keep_tiles_albion_by_crs_group_<group>.rds
##   - logs/keep_tiles_albion_by_crs_group_<group>.txt

albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table <- readRDS(
  file.path(pipeline_log_directory, "albion_tile_candidates_header_only.rds")
)

# For each CRS group, build footprints and intersect in that CRS
for (single_crs_group_label in unique(albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table$crs_group_label)) {

  albion_candidates_in_group_table <- albion_tile_candidates_header_only_table[
    crs_group_label == single_crs_group_label
  ]

  # CRS object for this group
  example_wkt_for_group <- albion_candidates_in_group_table$crs_wkt[1]
  crs_object_for_group  <- sf::st_crs(example_wkt_for_group)

  # Albion polygon transformed into this group CRS
  albion_polygon_in_group_crs <- sf::st_transform(study_area_polygon_albion, crs_object_for_group)

  # Build footprint polygons from header extents
  albion_candidate_footprints_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
    albion_candidates_in_group_table,
    coords = c("xmin","ymin"),
    crs = crs_object_for_group
  )

  albion_candidate_footprints_sf$geometry <- sf::st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(albion_candidates_in_group_table)), function(i) {
    sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
      c(albion_candidates_in_group_table$xmin[i], albion_candidates_in_group_table$ymin[i],
        albion_candidates_in_group_table$xmax[i], albion_candidates_in_group_table$ymin[i],
        albion_candidates_in_group_table$xmax[i], albion_candidates_in_group_table$ymax[i],
        albion_candidates_in_group_table$xmin[i], albion_candidates_in_group_table$ymax[i],
        albion_candidates_in_group_table$xmin[i], albion_candidates_in_group_table$ymin[i]),
      ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
    )))
  }), crs = crs_object_for_group)

  # True intersection
  albion_true_intersects_logical <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(albion_candidate_footprints_sf, albion_polygon_in_group_crs)) > 0

  albion_keep_tile_paths_in_group <- albion_candidate_footprints_sf$tile_path[albion_true_intersects_logical]

  cat("Albion true intersect tiles for", single_crs_group_label, ":", length(albion_keep_tile_paths_in_group), "\n")

  # Save keep list
  keep_list_rds_path <- file.path(
    pipeline_log_directory,
    paste0("keep_tiles_albion_by_crs_group_", single_crs_group_label, ".rds")
  )

  keep_list_txt_path <- file.path(
    pipeline_log_directory,
    paste0("keep_tiles_albion_by_crs_group_", single_crs_group_label, ".txt")
  )

  saveRDS(albion_keep_tile_paths_in_group, keep_list_rds_path)
  writeLines(albion_keep_tile_paths_in_group, keep_list_txt_path)
}

# showing only 191 tiles but QGIS shows 232 total for flights 17 and 14

######## 5A: Albion TRUE intersect from ALL UTM12 tiles (NO header rereads) ########
## Purpose:
##   - Remove any possibility that bbox-candidate logic dropped tiles
##   - Use existing lidar_header_inventory_table extents as footprints
##   - Produce authoritative counts by flight folder
##
## Inputs assumed to exist:
##   - lidar_header_inventory_table
##   - study_area_polygon_albion
##   - pipeline_log_directory


# 1) Identify the exact UTM12 CRS WKT from your distinct CRS table (no guessing)
utm12_geoid12B_wkt_string <- lidar_distinct_crs_table[
  grepl('UTM zone 12N', crs_wkt, fixed = TRUE) & grepl('Geoid12B', crs_wkt, fixed = TRUE),
  crs_wkt
][1]

if (is.na(utm12_geoid12B_wkt_string) || length(utm12_geoid12B_wkt_string) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find UTM zone 12N + Geoid12B CRS WKT in lidar_distinct_crs_table.")
}

utm12_geoid12B_crs_object <- sf::st_crs(utm12_geoid12B_wkt_string)

# 2) Subset header inventory to just UTM12 tiles (this should be LAZ + SouthernIdaho2018_14_LAZ)
utm12_tile_header_inventory_table <- lidar_header_inventory_table[
  header_read_ok == TRUE & crs_wkt == utm12_geoid12B_wkt_string
]

# 3) Transform Albion polygon into UTM12 CRS
albion_polygon_in_utm12_crs <- sf::st_transform(study_area_polygon_albion, utm12_geoid12B_crs_object)

# 4) Build footprint polygons from header extents (bbox polygons)
utm12_tile_footprints_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  utm12_tile_header_inventory_table,
  coords = c("xmin", "ymin"),
  crs = utm12_geoid12B_crs_object
)

utm12_tile_footprints_sf$geometry <- sf::st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(utm12_tile_header_inventory_table)), function(i) {
  sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$xmin[i], utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$ymin[i],
      utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$xmax[i], utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$ymin[i],
      utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$xmax[i], utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$ymax[i],
      utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$xmin[i], utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$ymax[i],
      utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$xmin[i], utm12_tile_header_inventory_table$ymin[i]),
    ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
  )))

## 3) Build footprint polygons helper (header-only)

build_bbox_footprints_from_header_table <- function(tile_header_table_in, crs_object_in) {

  tile_footprints_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(tile_header_table_in, coords = c("xmin","ymin"), crs = crs_object_in)

  tile_footprints_sf$geometry <- sf::st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tile_header_table_in)), function(i) {
    sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
      c(tile_header_table_in$xmin[i], tile_header_table_in$ymin[i],
        tile_header_table_in$xmax[i], tile_header_table_in$ymin[i],
        tile_header_table_in$xmax[i], tile_header_table_in$ymax[i],
        tile_header_table_in$xmin[i], tile_header_table_in$ymax[i],
        tile_header_table_in$xmin[i], tile_header_table_in$ymin[i]),
      ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
    )))
  }), crs = crs_object_in)

  tile_footprints_sf
}

    "{ORIGINALFILENAME}_{ID}_filtered"

#### Albion Filter Function (later we will use one function and apply to both areas) ####
  
   albion_filter_function <- function(x, ...) {
    tryCatch({

      if (inherits(x, "LAScluster")) x <- lidR::readLAS(x)
      if (is.null(x) || lidR::is.empty(x)) return(NULL)

      x <- lidR::filter_poi(x, !Withheld_flag & !Synthetic_flag)
      x <- lidR::classify_noise(x, lidR::ivf(res = 4, n = 12))
      x <- lidR::filter_poi(x, !Classification %in% c(7L, 18L))

      if (lidR::is.empty(x)) return(NULL)
      x

    }, error = function(e) {

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        "- Albion filter ERROR:",
        conditionMessage(e),
        "\n",
        file = file.path(albion_log_directory, "albion_filter_errors.txt"),
        append = TRUE
      )

      NULL
    })
   }
  
#### Step 8 Run Filter #####
  
   albion_filter_apply_result <- lidR::catalog_apply(albion_las_catalog_for_filtering, albion_filter_function)
  print(albion_filter_apply_result)

  cat("Albion filtering complete. Outputs in:\n", albion_filtered_output_directory, "\n")
}
  
#### Step 9 Post-run QA ####

)
```

## Find Only Tiles in Study Area

We do not want to process the entire dataset. We ONLY want those that fall within our study area, so we are going to use the st_intersection function to find only tiles in our study area. Instead of loading in every point cloud or cataloging all of the tiles, we are going to create a table that lists the bounding box of each LAZ/LAS file and use that to find which overlap.

```{r Find the Tiles!}
# Build a footprint (bbox polygon) for every LAZ/LAS using the header
study_union <- st_union(study_area)

# --- single pass header read (with tryCatch) ---
tile_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(tile_files, function(f) {
  tryCatch({
    h <- lidR::readLASheader(f)
    data.table(
      file = f,
      ok   = TRUE,
      xmin = h@PHB[["Min X"]],
      xmax = h@PHB[["Max X"]],
      ymin = h@PHB[["Min Y"]],
      ymax = h@PHB[["Max Y"]]
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    data.table(file = f, ok = FALSE)
  })
}), fill = TRUE)

# --- sanity: header failures ---
sum(!tile_dt$ok)
# Save immediately so you don’t redo this step
saveRDS(tile_dt, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/tile_dt_headers.rds")

# --- sanity: bad extents ---
bad_extent <- tile_dt[ok == TRUE & (xmax <= xmin | ymax <= ymin | is.na(xmin) | is.na(ymin))]
nrow(bad_extent)
# Optional: save a list of problematic files
if (nrow(bad_extent) > 0) {
  writeLines(bad_extent$file, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/bad_extent_files.txt")
}

# --- build polygons only for good headers ---
tile_ok <- tile_dt[ok == TRUE]

tile_sf <- st_as_sf(tile_ok, coords = c("xmin","ymin"), crs = crs_lidar) # dummy
tile_sf$geometry <- st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tile_ok)), function(i) {
  st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymin[i],
      tile_ok$xmax[i], tile_ok$ymin[i],
      tile_ok$xmax[i], tile_ok$ymax[i],
      tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymax[i],
      tile_ok$xmin[i], tile_ok$ymin[i]),
    ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE
  )))
}), crs = crs_lidar)

# --- sanity: CRS match ---
stopifnot(st_crs(tile_sf) == st_crs(study_union))

# --- intersects ---
hits <- st_intersects(tile_sf, study_union, sparse = FALSE)[, 1]
keep_files <- tile_sf$file[hits]

length(tile_files)
length(keep_files)

# Save keep list for tomorrow
saveRDS(keep_files, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/keep_files.rds")
writeLines(keep_files, "R:/CACR_HSM_LiDAR/04_logs/keep_files.txt")
```

```{r Full Area - Classification and Figuring Out Buggy Tiles :/}
# Small helper to prevent repeat list.files() later
list_filtered_tile_paths <- function(filtered_directory_path) {
  list.files(
    path = filtered_directory_path,
    pattern = "\\.(las|laz)$",
    full.names = TRUE,

##### 5) Helper: rename existing CSF outputs to stable names #####
# PURPOSE:
# Rename already-created CSF outputs that contain an extra catalog ID so they
# match the stable naming scheme:
#   tile_filtered_14_csf.las  ->  tile_filtered_csf.las

rename_csf_outputs_to_stable_names <- function(ground_directory_path) {

## I found that the pipeline was having trouble with the naming scheme that it was trying to generate. It was giving a ID to each tile after the filtering and classification step. This was creating snags in the pipeline as it wasn't connecting the filter tile to the classification that needed to be completed.
## IMPORTANT:
## This is the one-time cleanup step that fixes files already written with names like:
##   tile_filtered_1_csf.las
##   tile_filtered_2_csf.las
##
## and renames them to:
##   tile_filtered_csf.las
##
## This means:
## - DO NOT manually delete the already processed files
## - this function renames them in place
## - if a stable-name version already exists, it skips instead of overwriting

rename_csf_outputs_to_stable_names <- function(ground_directory_path) {
  existing_csf_output_paths <- list.files(
    ground_directory_path,
    pattern = "\\.(las|laz)$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  # Nothing to do if folder is empty
  if (length(existing_csf_output_paths) == 0) {
    message("No CSF outputs found in: ", ground_directory_path)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  existing_csf_output_base_names <- basename(existing_csf_output_paths)

  # Identify files that end in _<number>_csf.las or _<number>_csf.laz
  # Examples:
  #   tile_filtered_1_csf.las
  #   tile_filtered_22_csf.laz
  has_extra_catalog_id_logical <- grepl(
    "_[0-9]+_csf\\.(las|laz)$",
    existing_csf_output_base_names,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  output_paths_to_rename <- existing_csf_output_paths[has_extra_catalog_id_logical]

  if (length(output_paths_to_rename) == 0) {
    message("No CSF outputs need renaming in: ", ground_directory_path)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  for (single_old_path in output_paths_to_rename) {

    single_old_base_name <- basename(single_old_path)

    # Remove only the trailing _<number> immediately before _csf
    # Example:
    #   abc_filtered_14_csf.las -> abc_filtered_csf.las
    single_new_base_name <- sub(
      "_[0-9]+(_csf\\.(las|laz)$)",
      "\\1",
      single_old_base_name,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )

    single_new_path <- file.path(ground_directory_path, single_new_base_name)


    # Safety check:
    # if the stable target name already exists, skip so we do not overwrite files
    if (file.exists(single_new_path)) {
      warning(
        "Skipping rename because target already exists:\n",
        "  old: ", single_old_path, "\n",
        "  new: ", single_new_path
      )
      next
    }

    rename_successful <- file.rename(from = single_old_path, to = single_new_path)

    if (!rename_successful) {
      warning("Failed to rename: ", single_old_path)
    }
  }

  message("Finished renaming CSF outputs in: ", ground_directory_path)
}


##### 6) One-time rename of already processed CSF outputs #####
## Run this BEFORE the main loop so all existing outputs are standardized first

rename_csf_outputs_to_stable_names(albion_ground_output_directory)
rename_csf_outputs_to_stable_names(southhills_ground_output_directory)


##### 7) Helper: detect valid CSF outputs (resume-safe, stable naming version) #####

# PURPOSE:
# A filtered tile is considered done if:
# - filtered_stem + "_csf.las" exists OR filtered_stem + "_csf.laz" exists
# - and the output header is readable

## DONE means:
##  - exact expected output exists:
##      filtered_stem + "_csf.las"
##      OR filtered_stem + "_csf.laz"
##  - AND output header is readable
##
## This is much safer and simpler than wildcard matching once names are standardized

detect_valid_csf_outputs <- function(filtered_tile_paths, ground_dir) {

  filtered_stems <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filtered_tile_paths))

  has_valid_output <- vapply(filtered_stems, function(single_filtered_stem) {

    expected_las_output_path <- file.path(
      ground_dir,
      paste0(single_filtered_stem, "_csf.las")
    )

    expected_laz_output_path <- file.path(
      ground_dir,
      paste0(single_filtered_stem, "_csf.laz")
    )

    candidate_output_paths <- c(expected_las_output_path, expected_laz_output_path)
    candidate_output_paths <- candidate_output_paths[file.exists(candidate_output_paths)]


    # If neither .las nor .laz exists, this tile is not done
    if (length(candidate_output_paths) == 0) {
      return(FALSE)
    }
    
    # At least one existing candidate must have a readable header
    any(vapply(candidate_output_paths, function(single_output_path) {
      single_header <- try(lidR::readLASheader(single_output_path), silent = TRUE)
      !inherits(single_header, "try-error")
    }, logical(1)))

  }, logical(1))

  has_valid_output
}


##### 8) Helper: build CSF worker function #####
# PURPOSE:
# Build a catalog_apply() worker that classifies one tile/chunk and writes
# errors to a study-area-specific log instead of crashing the whole run.
## This is the function catalog_apply() runs on each tile/chunk.
## If a tile errors, we write the message to a study-area-specific log file
## and return NULL so the whole run does not crash immediately.

make_csf_ground_function <- function(study_area_name, log_directory_path, csf_algorithm_object) {

  dir.create(log_directory_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  csf_error_log_path <- file.path(
    log_directory_path,
    paste0(study_area_name, "_csf_ground_errors.txt")
  )

  function(cluster, ...) {
    tryCatch({

      las_object <- lidR::readLAS(cluster)

      if (is.null(las_object) || lidR::is.empty(las_object)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      las_object <- lidR::classify_ground(las_object, csf_algorithm_object)

      las_object

    }, error = function(e) {

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        "- ", study_area_name, " CSF ERROR: ",
        conditionMessage(e),
        "\n",
        sep = "",
        file = csf_error_log_path,
        append = TRUE
      )

      NULL
    })
  }
}

##### 10) MAIN LOOP: resume where it left off #####
## This is the main classification run.
## IMPORTANT CHANGE:
## output names now use:
##   {ORIGINALFILENAME}_csf
## NOT:
##   {ORIGINALFILENAME}_{ID}_csf
##
## That removes the extra chunk/catalog ID and keeps names stable.

for (single_run in study_area_run_list) {

  study_area_name <- single_run$study_area_name
  filtered_dir    <- single_run$filtered_dir
  ground_dir      <- single_run$ground_dir
  log_dir         <- single_run$log_dir

  cat("\n==============================\n")
  cat("Running CSF ground classification for:", study_area_name, "\n")
  cat("Filtered inputs:", filtered_dir, "\n")
  cat("Ground outputs :", ground_dir, "\n")
  cat("==============================\n\n")

  filtered_tile_paths <- list_filtered_tile_paths(filtered_dir)

  if (length(filtered_tile_paths) == 0) {
    warning("No filtered tiles found for ", study_area_name, " in: ", filtered_dir)
    next
  }

  cat(study_area_name, "filtered tiles found:", length(filtered_tile_paths), "\n")

  # Resume-safe skip logic using exact stable names
  already_done_logical <- detect_valid_csf_outputs(filtered_tile_paths, ground_dir)
  remaining_tile_paths <- filtered_tile_paths[!already_done_logical]

  cat(study_area_name, "tiles already ground-classified (valid):", sum(already_done_logical), "\n")
  cat(study_area_name, "tiles remaining to classify            :", length(remaining_tile_paths), "\n")

  saveRDS(
    remaining_tile_paths,
    file.path(log_dir, paste0(study_area_name, "_remaining_tiles_to_csf.rds"))
  )

  if (length(remaining_tile_paths) == 0) {
    message("All tiles already have valid CSF outputs for ", study_area_name, ". Skipping.")
    next
  }

  # Read only the remaining tiles into a LAScatalog
  ctg_remaining <- lidR::readLAScatalog(remaining_tile_paths)

  lidR::opt_chunk_size(ctg_remaining)   <- 0
  lidR::opt_chunk_buffer(ctg_remaining) <- 0

  # One file = one processing unit
  # chunk_size = 0 means use the original files directly
  lidR::opt_chunk_size(ctg_remaining)   <- 0
  lidR::opt_chunk_buffer(ctg_remaining) <- 0

  # Stable naming:
  # input:  tile_filtered.las
  # output: tile_filtered_csf.las
  lidR::opt_output_files(ctg_remaining) <- file.path(
    ground_dir,
    "{ORIGINALFILENAME}_csf"
  )

  # Use multiple cores at the catalog level
  # Keep lidR internal threads to 1 to avoid nested threading issues
  options(lidR.cores = 8)
  lidR::set_lidr_threads(1)

  csf_worker_function <- make_csf_ground_function(
    study_area_name      = study_area_name,
    log_directory_path   = log_dir,
    csf_algorithm_object = csf_ground_fullArea
  )

  csf_apply_result <- lidR::catalog_apply(ctg_remaining, csf_worker_function)
  print(csf_apply_result)

  cat("\nCSF classification finished for ", study_area_name, ". Outputs in:\n", ground_dir, "\n")
}

# Helper function: read LAS header safely and pull extent info
read_extent_from_header <- function(single_file_path) {

  single_header <- try(lidR::readLASheader(single_file_path), silent = TRUE)

  if (inherits(single_header, "try-error")) {
    return(data.frame(
      xmin = NA_real_,
      xmax = NA_real_,
      ymin = NA_real_,
      ymax = NA_real_,
      npoints_header = NA_real_,
      header_ok = FALSE
    ))
  }

  data.frame(
    xmin = single_header@PHB[["Min X"]],
    xmax = single_header@PHB[["Max X"]],
    ymin = single_header@PHB[["Min Y"]],
    ymax = single_header@PHB[["Max Y"]],
    npoints_header = single_header@PHB[["Number of point records"]],
    header_ok = TRUE
  )
}

  read_extent_from_header
)

  rbind,
  southhills_remaining_extent_list
)

  southhills_remaining_extent_table

#  Compare extents within repeated spatial tile code groups
## GOAL:
## For each repeated-code group, compare bounding boxes.
##
## We calculate:
## - area of file A
## - area of file B
## - overlap area
## - overlap proportion relative to the smaller file
##
## INTERPRETATION:
## overlap_proportion_near_1 = almost same footprint
## moderate overlap          = partial overlap
## near_0                    = likely not meaningfully overlapping

calculate_bbox_overlap <- function(xmin1, xmax1, ymin1, ymax1,
                                   xmin2, xmax2, ymin2, ymax2) {

  x_overlap <- max(0, min(xmax1, xmax2) - max(xmin1, xmin2))
  y_overlap <- max(0, min(ymax1, ymax2) - max(ymin1, ymin2))

  overlap_area <- x_overlap * y_overlap

  area1 <- (xmax1 - xmin1) * (ymax1 - ymin1)
  area2 <- (xmax2 - xmin2) * (ymax2 - ymin2)

  smaller_area <- min(area1, area2)

  overlap_proportion_smaller <- if (smaller_area > 0) overlap_area / smaller_area else NA_real_

  data.frame(
    area1 = area1,
    area2 = area2,
    overlap_area = overlap_area,
    overlap_proportion_smaller = overlap_proportion_smaller
  )
}

southhills_overlap_results <- list()

repeated_codes <- unique(southhills_repeated_groups_inventory$spatial_tile_code)

for (single_code in repeated_codes) {

  single_group <- southhills_repeated_groups_inventory[
    southhills_repeated_groups_inventory$spatial_tile_code == single_code,
  ]

  # Compare every pair within the group
  if (nrow(single_group) >= 2) {

    group_pairs <- utils::combn(seq_len(nrow(single_group)), 2)

    for (pair_index in seq_len(ncol(group_pairs))) {

      i <- group_pairs[1, pair_index]
      j <- group_pairs[2, pair_index]

      overlap_stats <- calculate_bbox_overlap(
        xmin1 = single_group$xmin[i],
        xmax1 = single_group$xmax[i],
        ymin1 = single_group$ymin[i],
        ymax1 = single_group$ymax[i],
        xmin2 = single_group$xmin[j],
        xmax2 = single_group$xmax[j],
        ymin2 = single_group$ymin[j],
        ymax2 = single_group$ymax[j]
      )

      southhills_overlap_results[[length(southhills_overlap_results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        spatial_tile_code = single_code,
        file_a = single_group$filtered_base[i],
        suffix_a = single_group$source_suffix[i],
        file_b = single_group$filtered_base[j],
        suffix_b = single_group$source_suffix[j],
        xmin_a = single_group$xmin[i],
        xmax_a = single_group$xmax[i],
        ymin_a = single_group$ymin[i],
        ymax_a = single_group$ymax[i],
        xmin_b = single_group$xmin[j],
        xmax_b = single_group$xmax[j],
        ymin_b = single_group$ymin[j],
        ymax_b = single_group$ymax[j],
        area_a = overlap_stats$area1,
        area_b = overlap_stats$area2,
        overlap_area = overlap_stats$overlap_area,
        overlap_proportion_smaller = overlap_stats$overlap_proportion_smaller,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }
}

# Helper: serial CSF run for supplied file list #####
## GOAL:
## Run one file at a time, write a log entry for each file,
## and avoid catalog_apply() while debugging South Hills.

run_csf_serial <- function(filtered_tile_paths, ground_directory_path, csf_algorithm_object, log_path) {

  for (single_tile_path in filtered_tile_paths) {

    single_tile_stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_tile_path))

    single_output_path <- file.path(
      ground_directory_path,
      paste0(single_tile_stem, "_csf.las")
    )

    # Skip if output already exists and has a readable header
    if (file.exists(single_output_path)) {
      single_existing_header <- try(lidR::readLASheader(single_output_path), silent = TRUE)

      if (!inherits(single_existing_header, "try-error")) {
        cat(
          format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
          " - SKIP already complete: ",
          single_tile_path, "\n",
          sep = "",
          file = log_path,
          append = TRUE
        )
        next
      }
    }

    cat(
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
      " - START: ",
      single_tile_path, "\n",
      sep = "",
      file = log_path,
      append = TRUE
    )

    tryCatch({

      single_las <- lidR::readLAS(single_tile_path)

      if (is.null(single_las) || lidR::is.empty(single_las)) {
        cat(
          format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
          " - EMPTY: ",
          single_tile_path, "\n",
          sep = "",
          file = log_path,
          append = TRUE
        )
        next
      }

      single_elapsed_time <- system.time({
        single_las <- lidR::classify_ground(single_las, csf_algorithm_object)
      })

      lidR::writeLAS(single_las, single_output_path)

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        " - DONE: ",
        single_tile_path,
        " --- elapsed_seconds=",
        round(single_elapsed_time["elapsed"], 2),
        "\n",
        sep = "",
        file = log_path,
        append = TRUE
      )

    }, error = function(e) {

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        " - ERROR: ",
        single_tile_path,
        " --- ",
        conditionMessage(e), "\n",
        sep = "",
        file = log_path,
        append = TRUE
      )
    })
  }
}

read_extent_from_header <- function(single_file_path) {

  single_header <- try(lidR::readLASheader(single_file_path), silent = TRUE)

  if (inherits(single_header, "try-error")) {
    return(data.table(
      xmin = NA_real_,
      xmax = NA_real_,
      ymin = NA_real_,
      ymax = NA_real_,
      npoints_header = NA_real_,
      header_ok = FALSE
    ))
  }

  data.table(
    xmin = single_header@PHB[["Min X"]],
    xmax = single_header@PHB[["Max X"]],
    ymin = single_header@PHB[["Min Y"]],
    ymax = single_header@PHB[["Max Y"]],
    npoints_header = single_header@PHB[["Number of point records"]],
    header_ok = TRUE
  )
}

    return(data.table(
      xmin = NA_real_,
      xmax = NA_real_,
      ymin = NA_real_,
      ymax = NA_real_,
      header_ok = FALSE

  data.table(
    xmin = single_header@PHB[["Min X"]],
    xmax = single_header@PHB[["Max X"]],
    ymin = single_header@PHB[["Min Y"]],
    ymax = single_header@PHB[["Max Y"]],
    header_ok = TRUE
  )
}

  southhills_unmatched_filtered_table,
  southhills_source_identity_with_extent_table,
  by.x = c("spatial_tile_code", "extent_signature"),
  by.y = c("tile_code", "extent_signature"),
  all.x = TRUE,
  allow.cartesian = TRUE
)

southhills_fallback_match_table[
  ,
  n_fallback_matches := .N,
  by = filtered_path
]

cat(
  "Fallback-matched filtered files:",
  southhills_fallback_match_table[!is.na(flight_name), uniqueN(filtered_path)],
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Still unmatched after fallback:",
  southhills_fallback_match_table[is.na(flight_name), uniqueN(filtered_path)],
  "\n"
)


##### 21) Combine Exact And Fallback Source Matches #####

southhills_exact_match_table <- southhills_filtered_source_join_table[
  !is.na(flight_name),
  .(
    filtered_path,
    filtered_base,
    filtered_stem,
    filtered_core,
    source_suffix,
    spatial_tile_code,
    flight_name,
    archived_base_name,
    zip_file_name,
    match_method = "exact_archived_name"
  )
]

southhills_fallback_match_clean_table <- southhills_fallback_match_table[
  !is.na(flight_name),
  .(
    filtered_path,
    filtered_base,
    filtered_stem,
    filtered_core,
    source_suffix,
    spatial_tile_code,
    flight_name,
    archived_base_name,
    zip_file_name,
    match_method = "tile_code_plus_extent"
  )
]

southhills_combined_source_match_table <- rbindlist(
  list(
    southhills_exact_match_table,
    southhills_fallback_match_clean_table
  ),
  fill = TRUE
)

southhills_combined_source_match_table <- unique(southhills_combined_source_match_table)

southhills_combined_source_match_table[
  ,
  n_total_matches := .N,
  by = filtered_path
]

print(
  southhills_combined_source_match_table[
    order(filtered_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      source_suffix,
      flight_name,
      archived_base_name,
      zip_file_name,
      match_method,
      n_total_matches
    )
  ][1:min(20, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_combined_source_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_source_match_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_combined_source_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_source_match_table.rds")
)

##### Attach Flight Identity To South Hills Remaining Inventory #####

# PURPOSE:
# Add the recovered source flight name back onto the main South Hills remaining
# inventory table so the inventory itself shows where each filtered tile came from.

southhills_inventory_flight_lookup_table <- unique(
  southhills_combined_source_match_table[
    ,
    .(
      filtered_path,
      flight_name,
      archived_base_name,
      zip_file_name,
      match_method,
      n_total_matches
    )
  ]
)

southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight <- merge(
  southhills_remaining_inventory,
  southhills_inventory_flight_lookup_table,
  by = "filtered_path",
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Reorder columns so flight info is easy to read
data.table::setcolorder(
  southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight,
  c(
    "filtered_path",
    "filtered_base",
    "spatial_tile_code",
    "source_suffix",
    "flight_name",
    "archived_base_name",
    "zip_file_name",
    "match_method",
    "n_total_matches",
    "xmin",
    "xmax",
    "ymin",
    "ymax",
    "npoints_header",
    "header_ok",
    "spatial_tile_count"
  )
)

cat(
  "Remaining South Hills files with recovered flight identity:",
  nrow(southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight),
  "\n"
)

print(
  southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight[
    order(spatial_tile_code, flight_name),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      source_suffix,
      flight_name,
      archived_base_name,
      zip_file_name,
      match_method,
      n_total_matches
    )
  ][1:min(30, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_remaining_extent_inventory_with_flight.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_remaining_inventory_with_flight,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_remaining_extent_inventory_with_flight.rds")
)

##### 22) Build Corrected Source Flight Labels From ZIP Names #####

# PURPOSE:
# The manifest join recovered candidate source rows, but some filtered files
# match multiple source rows. We therefore derive a corrected source-flight
# label from the ZIP file name and then ask whether each filtered tile has
# any Elko candidate source.

southhills_combined_source_match_table[
  ,
  source_flight_corrected := fifelse(
    grepl("Elko", zip_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "NorthWest_Elko_2020",
    fifelse(
      grepl("2018_12", zip_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
      "SouthernID_2018_12",
      fifelse(
        grepl("2018_14", zip_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
        "SouthernID_2018_14",
        fifelse(
          grepl("2018_15", zip_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
          "SouthernID_2018_15",
          fifelse(
            grepl("2018_17", zip_file_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
            "SouthernID_2018_17",
            NA_character_
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
]

print(
  southhills_combined_source_match_table[
    order(filtered_base, source_flight_corrected),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      zip_file_name,
      flight_name,
      source_flight_corrected,
      n_total_matches
    )
  ][1:min(30, .N)]
)


##### 23) Collapse Candidate Source Rows To One Record Per Filtered File #####
# The current join creates multiple candidate source rows per filtered file. This is likely due to confusion on which flight they come from. This is likely due to Elko having 2 different naming schemes (e.g., USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG200815 and USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG350605, the former being similar to the 2018 flights). We should be able to use our tiles from the All_Matched_Candidate_Tiles_Backup folder since the naming scheme denotes which flight file the tile originally came from.
# - SouthernID_2018_12__11TQG200815__ElkoNW2023_LAZ__USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG200815
# - NorthWest_Elko_2020__11TQG350605__ElkoNW2023_LAZ__USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG350605

# Before making overlap decisions, reduce each filtered file to a single summary row describing whether it is uniquely identified, ambiguous, etc.

southhills_file_source_summary_table <- southhills_combined_source_match_table[
  ,
  .(
    n_candidate_rows = .N,
    n_unique_candidate_sources = uniqueN(source_flight_corrected[!is.na(source_flight_corrected)]),
    candidate_sources = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(source_flight_corrected))), collapse = " | "),
    has_elko_candidate = any(source_flight_corrected == "NorthWest_Elko_2020", na.rm = TRUE),
    has_non_elko_candidate = any(
      !is.na(source_flight_corrected) &
        source_flight_corrected != "NorthWest_Elko_2020"
    )
  ),
  by = .(filtered_base)
]

southhills_file_source_summary_table[
  ,
  source_status := fifelse(
    has_elko_candidate & !has_non_elko_candidate,
    "unique_elko",
    fifelse(
      !has_elko_candidate & has_non_elko_candidate,
      "unique_non_elko",
      fifelse(
        has_elko_candidate & has_non_elko_candidate,
        "ambiguous_contains_elko",
        "unmatched"
      )
    )
  )
]

print(
  southhills_file_source_summary_table[
    order(filtered_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      n_candidate_rows,
      n_unique_candidate_sources,
      candidate_sources,
      has_elko_candidate,
      has_non_elko_candidate,
      source_status
    )
  ][1:min(30, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_file_source_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_file_source_summary_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_file_source_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_file_source_summary_table.rds")
)

##### 24) Audit Backup-Selected Raw File Names Against Filtered Files #####
# Here we can use the backup-selected raw tile folder names to recover cleaner provenance for the remaining South Hills filtered files.

# The current source-summary table is based on candidate matches from the manifest/join logic which is ambiguous.

# The backup-selected raw tile names appear to preserve more provenance: source flight label + tile code + zip/folder origin + original archived stem. If we can parse those names and link them back to the filtered files, we may be able to:
#   1. confirm the source identity for a filtered tile
#   2. reduce ambiguity
#   3. make the later keep/drop decision more trustworthy


# Define Backup-Selected Raw Tile Directory
# Note: this technically is all the backup tiles for both the South Hills and Albions, but we are simply naming it southhills since this is the region giving us trouble
southhills_backup_selected_directory <- file.path(
  project_root_directory,
  "01_raw_tiles_selected",
  "All_Matched_Candidate_Tiles_Backup"
)

if (!dir.exists(southhills_backup_selected_directory)) {
  stop(
    "Backup-selected raw tile directory not found: ",
    southhills_backup_selected_directory
  )
}


# List Backup-Selected Raw LAS/LAZ Files

southhills_backup_selected_paths <- list.files(
  southhills_backup_selected_directory,
  pattern = "\\.(las|laz)$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

cat(
  "Backup-selected raw LAS/LAZ files found:",
  length(southhills_backup_selected_paths),
  "\n"
)

if (length(southhills_backup_selected_paths) == 0) {
  stop("No LAS/LAZ files found in backup-selected raw tile directory.")
}


# Build Backup-Selected Raw Identity Table

# Parse backup-selected filenames using the correct field order:
#   FlightPathName__TileCode__SourceFlight__FullTileName.laz

# EXAMPLE:
#   SouthernID_2018_12__11TQG200875__ElkoNW2023_LAZ__USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG200875.laz
# WHICH MEANS:
#   1 = flight_path_name_from_backup   -> SouthernID_2018_12
#   2 = tile_code_from_backup          -> 11TQG200875
#   3 = source_flight_from_backup      -> ElkoNW2023_LAZ
#   4 = full_tile_name_from_backup     -> USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG200875
#
# IMPORTANT: We want SOURCE FLIGHT (part 3) for provenance decisions, not part 1.

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table <- data.table(
  backup_selected_path = southhills_backup_selected_paths,
  backup_selected_base = basename(southhills_backup_selected_paths)
)

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  backup_selected_stem := tools::file_path_sans_ext(backup_selected_base)
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  split_parts := strsplit(backup_selected_stem, "__", fixed = TRUE)
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  n_parts := lengths(split_parts)
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  flight_path_name_from_backup := vapply(
    split_parts,
    function(x) if (length(x) >= 1) x[1] else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  tile_code_from_backup := vapply(
    split_parts,
    function(x) if (length(x) >= 2) x[2] else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  source_flight_from_backup := vapply(
    split_parts,
    function(x) if (length(x) >= 3) x[3] else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  full_tile_name_from_backup := vapply(
    split_parts,
    function(x) if (length(x) >= 4) x[4] else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  source_flight_standardized := fifelse(
    grepl("Elko", source_flight_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "NorthWest_Elko_2020",
    fifelse(
      grepl("2018_12", source_flight_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
      "SouthernID_2018_12",
      fifelse(
        grepl("2018_14", source_flight_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
        "SouthernID_2018_14",
        fifelse(
          grepl("2018_15", source_flight_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
          "SouthernID_2018_15",
          fifelse(
            grepl("2018_17", source_flight_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
            "SouthernID_2018_17",
            NA_character_
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
]

southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
  ,
  split_parts := NULL
]

print(
  southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
    1:min(20, .N),
    .(
      backup_selected_base,
      flight_path_name_from_backup,
      tile_code_from_backup,
      source_flight_from_backup,
      source_flight_standardized,
      full_tile_name_from_backup,
      n_parts
    )
  ]
)

##### 25) Build One-Row-Per-File Backup Source Summary #####
# This will match the remaining South Hills filtered files to the backup-selected raw tile table, then collapse those matches to one summary row per filtered file.

# Build Lookup Table From Remaining Filtered Files --> to keep one clean row per remaining filtered file with the identifying fields we need for the backup audit join

southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table <- unique(
  southhills_filtered_identity_table[
    ,
    .(
      filtered_path,
      filtered_base,
      filtered_stem,
      filtered_core,
      spatial_tile_code
    )
  ]
)

print(
  southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table[
    1:min(20, .N),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      filtered_core,
      spatial_tile_code
    )
  ]
)


# Extract Short Tile Code From Filtered File Identity --> to recover the short tile code from the end of the full spatial tile code.

# EXAMPLE:
#   spatial_tile_code = USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG350875
#   short_tile_code   = 11TQG350875

# This is the field that should match tile_code_from_backup.

southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table[
  ,
  short_tile_code := regmatches(
    spatial_tile_code,
    regexpr("[0-9]{2}[A-Z]{3}[0-9]{6}$", spatial_tile_code)
  )
]

print(
  southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table[
    1:min(30, .N),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      short_tile_code
    )
  ]
)

cat(
  "Filtered files with extracted short tile code:",
  sum(!is.na(southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table$short_tile_code)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Filtered files missing short tile code:",
  sum(is.na(southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table$short_tile_code)),
  "\n"
)


# Match Remaining Filtered Files To Backup-Selected Rows --> join filtered files to the parsed backup-selected raw tile table using the short tile code, which should now be comparable across both tables.

# IMPORTANT:
# allow.cartesian = TRUE is intentional because one filtered file may match # more than one backup-selected row.

southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table <- merge(
  southhills_remaining_filtered_lookup_table,
  southhills_backup_selected_identity_table[
    ,
    .(
      backup_selected_path,
      backup_selected_base,
      tile_code_from_backup,
      source_flight_from_backup,
      source_flight_standardized,
      full_tile_name_from_backup,
      flight_path_name_from_backup
    )
  ],
  by.x = "short_tile_code",
  by.y = "tile_code_from_backup",
  all.x = TRUE,
  allow.cartesian = TRUE
)

# Count how many NON-MISSING backup matches each filtered file has.
southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  ,
  n_backup_matches := sum(!is.na(backup_selected_path)),
  by = filtered_path
]

cat(
  "Filtered files with at least one backup match:",
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
    !is.na(backup_selected_path),
    uniqueN(filtered_path)
  ],
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Filtered files with NO backup match:",
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
    is.na(backup_selected_path),
    uniqueN(filtered_path)
  ],
  "\n"
)

print(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
    order(filtered_base, source_flight_standardized),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      short_tile_code,
      source_flight_from_backup,
      source_flight_standardized,
      flight_path_name_from_backup,
      full_tile_name_from_backup,
      n_backup_matches
    )
  ][1:min(40, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_backup_match_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_backup_match_table.rds")
)

##### 26) Flag Source-Consistent Backup Matches #####
# Looking at the excel created in step 25, not all backup match rows are equally trustworthy. Some rows have a standardized source label that does NOT agree with the raw full tile name. For example:

#   source_flight_standardized = NorthWest_Elko_2020 --> full_tile_name_from_backup = USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG350875

# That is a weaker candidate than:
#   source_flight_standardized = NorthWest_Elko_2020 -->  full_tile_name_from_backup = USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG350875

# So here we explicitly flag whether the standardized source label agrees  with the full tile name.

southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  ,
  source_name_agrees_with_full_tile := fifelse(
    source_flight_standardized == "NorthWest_Elko_2020" &
      grepl("NorthWestElko|Elko", full_tile_name_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
    TRUE,
    fifelse(
      source_flight_standardized == "SouthernID_2018_12" &
        grepl("SouthernID_2018", full_tile_name_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
      TRUE,
      fifelse(
        source_flight_standardized == "SouthernID_2018_14" &
          grepl("SouthernID_2018", full_tile_name_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
        TRUE,
        fifelse(
          source_flight_standardized == "SouthernID_2018_15" &
            grepl("SouthernID_2018", full_tile_name_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
          TRUE,
          fifelse(
            source_flight_standardized == "SouthernID_2018_17" &
              grepl("SouthernID_2018", full_tile_name_from_backup, ignore.case = TRUE),
            TRUE,
            FALSE
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
]

print(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
    order(filtered_base, source_flight_standardized, full_tile_name_from_backup),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      short_tile_code,
      source_flight_from_backup,
      source_flight_standardized,
      full_tile_name_from_backup,
      source_name_agrees_with_full_tile,
      n_backup_matches
    )
  ][1:min(50, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_backup_match_table_with_consistency_flag.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_filtered_to_backup_match_table_with_consistency_flag.rds")
)

##### 27) Prefer Source-Consistent Backup Matches #####
# For each filtered file, prefer backup rows where the standardized source label agrees with the full tile name.

# RULES:
# - If a filtered file has at least one source-consistent backup row, keep only those source-consistent rows.
# - If a filtered file has no source-consistent rows, keep all rows so we do not accidentally discard all evidence for that file.

southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  ,
  any_consistent_match := any(source_name_agrees_with_full_tile, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = filtered_path
]

southhills_preferred_backup_match_table <- southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  any_consistent_match == FALSE | source_name_agrees_with_full_tile == TRUE
]

print(
  southhills_preferred_backup_match_table[
    order(filtered_base, source_flight_standardized, full_tile_name_from_backup),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      short_tile_code,
      source_flight_standardized,
      full_tile_name_from_backup,
      source_name_agrees_with_full_tile,
      any_consistent_match
    )
  ][1:min(50, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_preferred_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_preferred_backup_match_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_preferred_backup_match_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_preferred_backup_match_table.rds")
)

##### 27 QA) Preferred Backup Matches For Duplicates/Triplicates #####
# Inspect a small sample of duplicate/triplicate filtered files before and after the source-consistency filter so you can verify that mismatched candidate rows were removed and the more trustworthy rows were retained.

# WHAT THIS SHOWS:
# - BEFORE: all candidate backup rows for a filtered file
# - AFTER : only the preferred rows retained after step 27

# HOW TO READ IT:
# For a true Elko candidate row, you want to see something like:
#   source_flight_standardized = NorthWest_Elko_2020 --> full_tile_name_from_backup contains NorthWestElko / NV

# For a true SouthernID candidate row, you want to see something like:
#   source_flight_standardized = SouthernID_2018_12 (or 14/15/17) -->  full_tile_name_from_backup contains SouthernID / ID

# A mismatched row is something like:
#   source_flight_standardized = NorthWest_Elko_2020 --> but full_tile_name_from_backup is a SouthernID tile name


# Identify Filtered Files With More Than One Backup Candidate

southhills_multi_candidate_files <- unique(
  southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
    n_backup_matches > 1,
    .(filtered_base)
  ]
)

cat(
  "Filtered files with more than one backup candidate row:",
  nrow(southhills_multi_candidate_files),
  "\n"
)


# Select A Small QA Sample --> Grab a few duplicate/triplicate files to inspect.

southhills_qa_sample_filtered_bases <- southhills_multi_candidate_files[
  1:min(10, .N),
  filtered_base
]

print(southhills_qa_sample_filtered_bases)


# QA Table: BEFORE Preferred-Row Filtering
southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  ,
  any_consistent_match := any(source_name_agrees_with_full_tile, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = filtered_path
]

southhills_preferred_backup_match_table <- southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  any_consistent_match == FALSE | source_name_agrees_with_full_tile == TRUE
]

southhills_qa_before_preferred_table <- southhills_filtered_to_backup_match_table[
  filtered_base %in% southhills_qa_sample_filtered_bases,
  .(
    filtered_base,
    short_tile_code,
    source_flight_from_backup,
    source_flight_standardized,
    flight_path_name_from_backup,
    full_tile_name_from_backup,
    source_name_agrees_with_full_tile,
    any_consistent_match
  )
][order(filtered_base, source_flight_standardized, full_tile_name_from_backup)]

print(southhills_qa_before_preferred_table)

fwrite(
  southhills_qa_before_preferred_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_QA_before_preferred_rows.csv")
)


# QA Table: AFTER Preferred-Row Filtering

southhills_qa_after_preferred_table <- southhills_preferred_backup_match_table[
  filtered_base %in% southhills_qa_sample_filtered_bases,
  .(
    filtered_base,
    short_tile_code,
    source_flight_from_backup,
    source_flight_standardized,
    flight_path_name_from_backup,
    full_tile_name_from_backup,
    source_name_agrees_with_full_tile,
    any_consistent_match
  )
][order(filtered_base, source_flight_standardized, full_tile_name_from_backup)]

print(southhills_qa_after_preferred_table)

##### 28) Collapse Preferred Backup Matches To One Row Per Filtered File #####
# Summarize the preferred backup-source evidence for each filtered file into one row.

# INTERPRETATION:
# - unique_elko = only Elko source found
# - unique_non_elko = only non-Elko source found
# - ambiguous_contains_elko = both Elko and non-Elko sources found
# - unmatched = no usable backup match found

southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table <- southhills_preferred_backup_match_table[
  ,
  .(
    n_backup_match_rows = sum(!is.na(backup_selected_path)),
    n_unique_backup_sources = uniqueN(source_flight_standardized[!is.na(source_flight_standardized)]),
    backup_candidate_sources = paste(
      sort(unique(na.omit(source_flight_standardized))),
      collapse = " | "
    ),
    backup_raw_source_labels = paste(
      sort(unique(na.omit(source_flight_from_backup))),
      collapse = " | "
    ),
    backup_flight_path_names = paste(
      sort(unique(na.omit(flight_path_name_from_backup))),
      collapse = " | "
    ),
    backup_full_tile_names = paste(
      sort(unique(na.omit(full_tile_name_from_backup))),
      collapse = " | "
    ),
    backup_has_elko = any(source_flight_standardized == "NorthWest_Elko_2020", na.rm = TRUE),
    backup_has_non_elko = any(
      !is.na(source_flight_standardized) &
        source_flight_standardized != "NorthWest_Elko_2020"
    )
  ),
  by = .(filtered_path, filtered_base, spatial_tile_code, short_tile_code)
]

southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table[
  ,
  backup_source_status := fifelse(
    backup_has_elko & !backup_has_non_elko,
    "unique_elko",
    fifelse(
      !backup_has_elko & backup_has_non_elko,
      "unique_non_elko",
      fifelse(
        backup_has_elko & backup_has_non_elko,
        "ambiguous_contains_elko",
        "unmatched"
      )
    )
  )
]

print(
  southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table[
    order(filtered_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      spatial_tile_code,
      short_tile_code,
      n_backup_match_rows,
      n_unique_backup_sources,
      backup_candidate_sources,
      backup_raw_source_labels,
      backup_flight_path_names,
      backup_full_tile_names,
      backup_source_status
    )
  ][1:min(40, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_backup_file_source_summary_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_backup_file_source_summary_table.rds")
)

##### 29) Attach Cleaned Backup Source Summary To Overlap Pairs #####
# Join the cleaned one-row-per-file backup source summary onto both sides of each already-computed overlap pair.

# IMPORTANT:
# We are NOT recomputing overlap here (see step 15) rather we are using the overlap values already stored in: southhills_overlap_results_table

southhills_overlap_pair_source_table <- merge(
  southhills_overlap_results_table,
  southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table[
    ,
    .(
      filtered_base,
      source_status_a = backup_source_status,
      candidate_sources_a = backup_candidate_sources,
      raw_source_labels_a = backup_raw_source_labels,
      full_tile_names_a = backup_full_tile_names,
      has_elko_a = backup_has_elko,
      has_non_elko_a = backup_has_non_elko
    )
  ],
  by.x = "file_a",
  by.y = "filtered_base",
  all.x = TRUE
)

southhills_overlap_pair_source_table <- merge(
  southhills_overlap_pair_source_table,
  southhills_backup_file_source_summary_table[
    ,
    .(
      filtered_base,
      source_status_b = backup_source_status,
      candidate_sources_b = backup_candidate_sources,
      raw_source_labels_b = backup_raw_source_labels,
      full_tile_names_b = backup_full_tile_names,
      has_elko_b = backup_has_elko,
      has_non_elko_b = backup_has_non_elko
    )
  ],
  by.x = "file_b",
  by.y = "filtered_base",
  all.x = TRUE
)

print(
  southhills_overlap_pair_source_table[
    order(-overlap_proportion_smaller, spatial_tile_code),
    .(
      spatial_tile_code,
      file_a,
      source_status_a,
      candidate_sources_a,
      file_b,
      source_status_b,
      candidate_sources_b,
      overlap_proportion_smaller
    )
  ][1:min(40, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_overlap_pair_source_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_overlap_pair_source_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_overlap_pair_source_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_overlap_pair_source_table.rds")
)
```

### Solution to Overlap/Duplicates

I figured out the solution, but I think it is valuable to keep these steps above as a troubleshooting guide and also to help explain how I got to this.

Earlier in the code above, R identified that in our 01_raw_tiles_selected we sometimes had triplicates but in the buggy tiles that wouldn't process it only flagged two of these three. For example: if we look at tile code 11TQG350875. R flags three tiles that have this code:

1.  SouthernID_2018_12\_\_11TQG350875\_\_SouthernIdaho2018_12_Part21_LAZ\_\_USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG350875
2.  SouthernID_2018_12\_\_11TQG350875\_\_ElkoNW2023_LAZ\_\_USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG350875
3.  SouthernID_2018_12\_\_11TQG350875\_\_ElkoNW2023_LAZ\_\_USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG350875

However, later when comparing this to our overlapping buggy tiles that wouldn't classify, R only shows the two that share the same file name: USGS_LPC_ID_SouthernID_2018_D19_11TQG350875. This made me wonder if the tile with a different name processed in the ground classification and if it covered the same area as the other two. To check this, I started by simply searched the 02_ground_csf folder to see if USGS_LPC_NV_NorthWestElko_2020_D20_11TQG350875 processed and found that it had. Then, I opened all three of these tiles in CloudCompare and I found that the tiles that share the same exact name also cover the exact same area. The tiles that has the more unique name not only covered the same area but also more of the surrounding area.

Given this, we can look at our buggy tiles (158) and for the ones where they share a tile code with the elko flights check to see if they processed already but under the more unique elko naming style and, if so, look to see if the extent of the elko flight tile overlaps/surpasses the buggy tiles.

Based on the excel sheets made I suspect that of the 158 buggy tiles, 72 of them are likely processed under the elko unique name while 86 of them seem to be overlaps between SouthernID_2018_12 and SouthernID_2018_15 in which case we can just pick one if they are a complete overlap or keep both if it's only a partial.

I am going to keep the number going from the previous chunk.

```{r Audit and Handling Buggy Tiles}
##### 30) Build Inventory Of Already-Classified South Hills CSF Outputs #####

southhills_existing_csf_output_paths <- list.files(
  southhills_ground_output_directory,
  pattern = "\\.(las|laz)$",

southhills_existing_csf_inventory_table[

southhills_existing_csf_inventory_table[

southhills_existing_csf_inventory_table[

southhills_existing_csf_inventory_table[

print(

# WHY:

    )

)

southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table <- merge(

)

print(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table[
    order(filtered_base, csf_output_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      short_tile_code,
      csf_output_base,
      backup_source_status,
      backup_source_status_existing
    )
  ][1:min(40, .N)]
)

##### 34) Calculate Overlap Between Buggy Tiles And Already-Classified Outputs #####
# Quantify how much each remaining buggy tile overlaps any already-classified CSF output with the same short tile code.

southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_list <- vector(
  "list",
  nrow(southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table)
)

for (row_index in seq_len(nrow(southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table))) {

  single_row <- southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table[row_index]

  if (
    is.na(single_row$bug_xmin) || is.na(single_row$csf_xmin) ||
    is.na(single_row$bug_ymin) || is.na(single_row$csf_ymin)
  ) {
    southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_list[[row_index]] <- data.table(
      overlap_area = NA_real_,
      overlap_proportion_smaller = NA_real_
    )
    next
  }

  single_overlap <- calculate_bbox_overlap(
    xmin1 = single_row$bug_xmin,
    xmax1 = single_row$bug_xmax,
    ymin1 = single_row$bug_ymin,
    ymax1 = single_row$bug_ymax,
    xmin2 = single_row$csf_xmin,
    xmax2 = single_row$csf_xmax,
    ymin2 = single_row$csf_ymin,
    ymax2 = single_row$csf_ymax
  )

  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_list[[row_index]] <- single_overlap[
    ,
    .(
      overlap_area,
      overlap_proportion_smaller
    )
  ]
}

southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_table <- rbindlist(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_list,
  fill = TRUE
)

southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table <- cbind(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table,
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_overlap_table
)

print(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table[
    order(-overlap_proportion_smaller, filtered_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      short_tile_code,
      csf_output_base,
      backup_source_status,
      backup_source_status_existing,
      overlap_proportion_smaller
    )
  ][1:min(60, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table.rds")
)

##### 35) Summarize Whether Buggy Tiles Are Already Covered By Classified Outputs #####
# Reduce the buggy-vs-existing comparison to one row per buggy tile.

# INTERPRETATION:
# - already_covered_by_classified_elko: a classified output with Elko evidence covers the buggy tile at near-complete overlap

# - already_covered_by_classified_non_elko: no classified Elko coverage, but a classified non-Elko output covers it

# - not_already_covered: no near-complete classified coverage found

southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table <- southhills_buggy_vs_existing_matches_table[
  ,
  .(
    max_overlap_with_existing = suppressWarnings(max(overlap_proportion_smaller, na.rm = TRUE)),
    covered_by_existing_elko = any(
      overlap_proportion_smaller >= 0.98 &
        backup_has_elko_existing == TRUE,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    covered_by_existing_non_elko = any(
      overlap_proportion_smaller >= 0.98 &
        backup_has_elko_existing != TRUE &
        !is.na(csf_output_base),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n_existing_matches = sum(!is.na(csf_output_base))
  ),
  by = .(
    filtered_path,
    filtered_base,
    short_tile_code,
    backup_source_status
  )
]

southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table[
  is.infinite(max_overlap_with_existing),
  max_overlap_with_existing := NA_real_
]

southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table[
  ,
  coverage_status := fifelse(
    covered_by_existing_elko,
    "already_covered_by_classified_elko",
    fifelse(
      covered_by_existing_non_elko,
      "already_covered_by_classified_non_elko",
      "not_already_covered"
    )
  )
]

print(
  southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table[
    order(coverage_status, filtered_base),
    .(
      filtered_base,
      short_tile_code,
      backup_source_status,
      max_overlap_with_existing,
      n_existing_matches,
      coverage_status
    )
  ][1:min(60, .N)]
)

fwrite(
  southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_buggy_coverage_summary_table.csv")
)

saveRDS(
  southhills_buggy_coverage_summary_table,
  file.path(southhills_log_directory, "SouthHills_buggy_coverage_summary_table.rds")
)

##### 39) Restrict Overlap Decision Table To Buggy Tiles Not Already Covered #####
# We already know the 58 covered tiles can be skipped. So now we only need to apply overlap-based keep/drop logic to the remaining 100.

southhills_overlap_decision_table <- copy(southhills_overlap_pair_source_table)

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  overlap_class := fifelse(
    overlap_proportion_smaller >= 0.98,
    "near_complete_overlap",
    "partial_overlap"
  )
]

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  source_rank_a := fifelse(
    source_status_a == "unique_elko", 3L,
    fifelse(
      source_status_a == "ambiguous_contains_elko", 2L,
      fifelse(
        source_status_a == "unique_non_elko", 1L,
        0L
      )
    )
  )
]

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  source_rank_b := fifelse(
    source_status_b == "unique_elko", 3L,
    fifelse(
      source_status_b == "ambiguous_contains_elko", 2L,
      fifelse(
        source_status_b == "unique_non_elko", 1L,
        0L
      )
    )
  )
]

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  preferred_file := fifelse(
    overlap_class == "partial_overlap",
    NA_character_,
    fifelse(
      source_rank_a > source_rank_b,
      file_a,
      fifelse(
        source_rank_b > source_rank_a,
        file_b,
        pmin(file_a, file_b)
      )
    )
  )
]

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  drop_file := fifelse(
    overlap_class == "partial_overlap",
    NA_character_,
    fifelse(
      preferred_file == file_a,
      file_b,
      file_a
    )
  )
]

cat("Overlap decision rows:", nrow(southhills_overlap_decision_table), "\n")

southhills_buggy_remaining_overlap_decision_table <- southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  file_a %in% southhills_buggy_not_covered_table$filtered_base |
    file_b %in% southhills_buggy_not_covered_table$filtered_base
]

cat(
  "Overlap decision rows involving buggy tiles not already covered:",
  nrow(southhills_buggy_remaining_overlap_decision_table),
  "\n"
)

# Add Decision Reason Back To Overlap Decision Table

southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  ,
  decision_reason := fifelse(
    overlap_class == "partial_overlap",
    "keep_both_partial_overlap",
    fifelse(
      source_rank_a > source_rank_b & source_rank_a == 3L,
      "keep_unique_elko_drop_lower_rank",
      fifelse(
        source_rank_b > source_rank_a & source_rank_b == 3L,
        "keep_unique_elko_drop_lower_rank",
        fifelse(
          source_rank_a > source_rank_b & source_rank_a == 2L,
          "keep_ambiguous_elko_drop_unique_non_elko",
          fifelse(
            source_rank_b > source_rank_a & source_rank_b == 2L,
            "keep_ambiguous_elko_drop_unique_non_elko",
            "keep_one_near_complete_overlap_deterministic"
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
]

southhills_buggy_remaining_overlap_decision_table <- southhills_overlap_decision_table[
  file_a %in% southhills_buggy_not_covered_table$filtered_base |
    file_b %in% southhills_buggy_not_covered_table$filtered_base
]

print(
  southhills_buggy_remaining_overlap_decision_table[
    order(-overlap_proportion_smaller, spatial_tile_code),
    .(
      spatial_tile_code,
      file_a,
      source_status_a,
      source_rank_a,
      file_b,
      source_status_b,
      source_rank_b,
      overlap_proportion_smaller,
      overlap_class,
      preferred_file,
      drop_file,
      decision_reason
    )
  ][1:min(40, .N)]
)

##### 40) Build Final Keep/Drop Tables For Buggy Tiles Not Already Covered #####
```

```{r Classy Remaining Tiles - Post Debugging}
##### Define Serial CSF Helper Function #####
# Classify one filtered LAS/LAZ tile at a time and write the CSF output.
#
# WHY WE USE THIS HERE:
# These South Hills tiles are the exact subset that caused issues in the catalog-based workflow, so we process them one-by-one to avoid those overlap/catalog problems.
#
# WHAT THIS FUNCTION DOES:
# 1. Loops through each filtered tile path
# 2. Skips tiles that already have a valid CSF output
# 3. Reads the tile
# 4. Runs CSF ground classification
# 5. Writes the classified output to 02_ground_csf
# 6. Logs START / DONE / SKIP / ERROR messages to a text log

run_csf_serial <- function(filtered_tile_paths,
                           ground_directory_path,
                           csf_algorithm_object,
                           log_path) {

  for (single_tile_path in filtered_tile_paths) {

    single_tile_stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(single_tile_path))

    single_output_path <- file.path(
      ground_directory_path,
      paste0(single_tile_stem, "_csf.las")
    )

    # Skip tiles that already have a readable CSF output
    if (file.exists(single_output_path)) {

      single_existing_header <- try(
        lidR::readLASheader(single_output_path),
        silent = TRUE
      )

      if (!inherits(single_existing_header, "try-error")) {
        cat(
          format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
          " - SKIP already complete: ",
          single_tile_path,
          "\n",
          sep = "",
          file = log_path,
          append = TRUE
        )
        next
      }
    }

    # Log start of processing
    cat(
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
      " - START: ",
      single_tile_path,
      "\n",
      sep = "",
      file = log_path,
      append = TRUE
    )

    tryCatch({

      single_las <- lidR::readLAS(single_tile_path)

      if (is.null(single_las) || lidR::is.empty(single_las)) {
        cat(
          format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
          " - EMPTY: ",
          single_tile_path,
          "\n",
          sep = "",
          file = log_path,
          append = TRUE
        )
        next
      }

      single_elapsed_time <- system.time({
        single_las <- lidR::classify_ground(single_las, csf_algorithm_object)
      })

      lidR::writeLAS(single_las, single_output_path)

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        " - DONE: ",
        single_tile_path,
        " --- elapsed_seconds=",
        round(single_elapsed_time["elapsed"], 2),
        "\n",
        sep = "",
        file = log_path,
        append = TRUE
      )

    }, error = function(e) {

      cat(
        format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        " - ERROR: ",
        single_tile_path,
        " --- ",
        conditionMessage(e),
        "\n",
        sep = "",
        file = log_path,
        append = TRUE
      )
    })
  }
}
```
